Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, let $\mathfrak h$ be any Cartan subalgebra in the
nilpotent self-normalizing sense, and fix a positive root system with Weyl
group $W$ and half-sum $\rho$ of its positive roots. The shifted Harish-Chandra map

$$ \operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S(\mathfrak h)^W, \qquad \operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(\lambda)=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda-\rho), $$

is an algebra isomorphism.

Fix a triangular decomposition $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak n^-\oplus \mathfrak h\oplus \mathfrak n^+$ from [[thm-triangular-decomposition-from-a-chosen-positive-root-system]]. By the PBW basis from [[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]], multiplication gives a vector-space decomposition

$$U(\mathfrak g)=U(\mathfrak h)\oplus \bigl(\mathfrak n^-U(\mathfrak g)+U(\mathfrak g)\mathfrak n^+\bigr).$$

The projection onto the first summand is the **Harish-Chandra projection**

$$\operatorname{pr}\colon U(\mathfrak g)_0\to U(\mathfrak h)=S(\mathfrak h),$$

where $U(\mathfrak g)_0$ denotes the zero-weight subspace for the adjoint action of $\mathfrak h$.

For central elements $z,z'\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$, the Harish-Chandra projection from [[def-harish-chandra-projection]] satisfies

$$\operatorname{pr}(zz')=\operatorname{pr}(z)\operatorname{pr}(z').$$

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module with highest vector $v$ of weight $\lambda$, and let $z\in Z(U(\mathfrak g))$. Then

$$zv=\operatorname{pr}(z)(\lambda)\,v,$$

so the scalar by which $z$ acts on $M$ is obtained by evaluating the Harish-Chandra projection at $\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a chosen positive-root system and corresponding Borel, Weyl group $W$, and half-sum $\rho$ of positive roots. Let $\chi_\lambda$ and $\chi_\mu$ be the central characters obtained from highest weights $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ for this Borel. Then

$$\chi_\lambda=\chi_\mu \quad \text{if and only if} \quad \mu\in W\cdot \lambda,$$

where $W\cdot \lambda:=\{w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho : w\in W\}$.

Let $M$ be a cyclic highest-weight module of highest weight $\lambda$. Then the quadratic Casimir element acts on $M$ by the scalar

$$ (\lambda,\lambda+2\rho), $$

where the pairing on $\mathfrak h^*$ is induced by the Killing form and $\rho$ is the Weyl vector from [[def-weyl-vector-rho-for-a-chosen-positive-system]].

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$ and $\beta\in Q^+$, let $K(\gamma)$ be the
number of partitions of $\gamma\in Q^+$ into positive roots, and set
$K(\gamma)=0$ when $\gamma\notin Q^+$. Then

$$D_\beta(\lambda)\doteq\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\prod_{n\ge1}(\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle-n)^{K(\beta-n\alpha)}.$$

For fixed $\beta$ only finitely many exponents are nonzero.

Fix $\alpha\in\Phi^+$ and $n\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, and let
$H_{\alpha,n}=\{\lambda:\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle=n\}$.
Suppose $H_{\alpha,n}$ is a factor hyperplane of at least one
Shapovalov determinant. Outside a countable union of proper affine
subspaces of $H_{\alpha,n}$, put $\mu=\lambda-n\alpha$.
Then $M(\mu)$ is simple, there is a unique one-dimensional space of maps
$M(\mu)\to M(\lambda)$, every nonzero such map is injective, and its image
is the entire Shapovalov radical $J(\lambda)$. Consequently
$M(\lambda)/M(\mu)=L(\lambda)$ is simple and

$$\dim\ker S_\lambda|_{M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\beta}}=K(\beta-n\alpha)$$

for every $\beta\in Q^+$, with $K(\eta)=0$ outside $Q^+$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in the real span
$E$ of the roots with its $W$-invariant positive definite form, and let $\xi$
and $\eta$ be weights in $E$ that are dominant, so
$\langle\xi,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\ge0$ and
$\langle\eta,\alpha_i^\vee\rangle\ge0$ for every simple root $\alpha_i$
([[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]). Then
$$\lvert\xi-w\eta\rvert\ge\lvert\xi-\eta\rvert\qquad\text{for every }w\in W,$$
and equality holds if and only if $w\eta$ lies in the set
$W_\xi\eta=\{v\eta:v\in W_\xi\}$, where $W_\xi=\{v\in W:v\xi=\xi\}$ is the
stabilizer of $\xi$. In particular, if $\xi$ is regular, so that
$W_\xi=\{1\}$, then equality forces $w\eta=\eta$; if $\xi=0$ then equality
holds for every $w$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\nu$ be a dominant
integral weight
([[def-integral-dominant-and-strictly-dominant-weights]]) and let $\gamma$ be
a weight of the finite-dimensional simple module $L(\nu)$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]]).
Then, in the $W$-invariant positive definite form on the real span $E$ of the
roots ([[prop-the-roots-form-a-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]]),
$$\lvert\gamma\rvert\le\lvert\nu\rvert,$$
with equality if and only if $\gamma$ lies in the Weyl orbit $W\nu$; moreover
every weight in $W\nu$ occurs in $L(\nu)$ with multiplicity one.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

Restricted Chevalley duality is an exact contravariant equivalence $D:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O^{\mathrm{op}}$, with a natural isomorphism $D^2\cong\operatorname{id}$. It preserves each weight-space dimension, the formal character, and every simple composition multiplicity.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The simple objects of $\mathcal O$ are exactly the modules $L(\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$, and $L(\lambda)\cong L(\mu)$ if and only if $\lambda=\mu$. Simplicity here excludes zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every simple object
$L(\mu)$ of $\mathcal O$ admits a projective cover
$P(\mu)\twoheadrightarrow L(\mu)$
([[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]), which may be chosen
inside the linkage class of $\mu$; the cover is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable. Consequently $\mathcal O$ has enough projectives: every object
of $\mathcal O$ is a quotient of a finite direct sum of such projective
covers, because objects of $\mathcal O$ have finite length and each composition
factor is a quotient of its projective cover.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If a projective object
$P$ of $\mathcal O$ admits an epimorphism $P\twoheadrightarrow L$ onto a
simple object $L$, then some indecomposable direct summand of $P$ maps onto
$L$, and that summand is a projective cover of $L$ (an essential epimorphism
with projective source, [[def-essential-epimorphism-and-projective-cover]]).
Any two projective covers of $L$ are isomorphic, although not canonically so,
and the endomorphism ring of a projective cover is local. In particular, for
every simple $L$ there is at most one isomorphism class of indecomposable
projectives with head $L$; when such a cover exists it is written $P(L)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Every projective object
of $\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

More precisely, each projective cover $P(\mu)$ produced by
[[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]] is a direct summand of the
projective object $\operatorname{pr}_C(E\otimes M(\lambda))$ of
[[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]], which is a
direct summand of $E\otimes M(\lambda)$; a general projective object has
finite length, hence is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives,
each of which is a projective cover of its simple head.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For all weights
$\lambda$ and $\mu$,
$$(P(\lambda):\Delta(\mu))=[\Delta(\mu):L(\lambda)]=[M(\mu):L(\lambda)],$$
where $P(\lambda)$ is the projective cover of $L(\lambda)$, the left-hand
multiplicity is the Verma-flag multiplicity of
[[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]], and the right-hand
multiplicity is the simple composition multiplicity of the Verma module
$M(\mu)$ ([[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

For weights $\lambda,\mu$, a nonzero homomorphism $M(\mu)\to M(\lambda)$ exists if and only if $\mu\uparrow\lambda$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module with weight
multiplicities $\dim E_\eta$
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]). For every
weight $\mu$, the object $E\otimes\Delta(\mu)$ has a finite Verma flag
([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]) whose factors are $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$,
the factor $\Delta(\mu+\eta)$ occurring $\dim E_\eta$ times; the factors can be
ordered so that a real-linear height $\ell$ with $\ell(\alpha_i)=1$ is nonincreasing.

Consequently, if $X\in\mathcal O$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(\nu))$, then $E\otimes X$ has a finite Verma flag and
$$(E\otimes X:\Delta(\mu))=\sum_\eta\dim E_\eta\,(X:\Delta(\mu-\eta)).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $P$ be a projective
object of $\mathcal O$ ([[def-projective-object]]) and let $E$ be a
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module
([[def-weight-and-weight-space-of-a-lie-algebra-representation]]). Then
$E\otimes P$ belongs to $\mathcal O$ and is projective in $\mathcal O$.

The same tensor adjunction shows that if $I$ is injective in $\mathcal O$,
then $E\otimes I$ is injective.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ the
translation functor $T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]) is exact, and
$T_{\chi',E^*,\chi}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of
$T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$; in particular both functors send projectives to
projectives and injectives to injectives. Consequently, in the setting of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], $T_\mu^\lambda$ is both a left
and a right adjoint of $T_\lambda^\mu$, and the two functors are exact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and a fixed
positive system, let $\lambda$ be dominant integral, let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$
be the finite-dimensional irreducible module of highest weight $\lambda$, and
let $w_0$ be the longest element of the Weyl group
([[def-length-and-longest-element-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]). Then the dual
module $V(\lambda)^*$
([[prop-direct-sum-dual-hom-and-tensor-representations]]) is irreducible and
has highest weight
$$-w_0(\lambda).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

For a linkage class $C=W_\lambda\cdot\lambda$, let $\mathcal O_C$ be the full subcategory of objects all of whose simple composition factors have labels in $C$. Then $\mathcal O=\bigoplus_C\mathcal O_C$, and each nonzero $\mathcal O_C$ is indecomposable as a categorical direct summand. These are precisely the blocks. Each $\mathcal O_C$ lies in $\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}$; a central-character summand can contain several blocks. Independently, grouping weights by cosets of the root lattice $Q$ gives a canonical coarser decomposition by weight cosets.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $C$ be a linkage
class and let $\operatorname{pr}_C:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_C$ be the exact
projection of the block decomposition of
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]], i.e. the functor
that keeps the direct summand supported on $C$.

If $P\in\mathcal O$ is projective
([[def-projective-object]]), then $\operatorname{pr}_C(P)$ is projective in
$\mathcal O$. Conversely, if $Q\in\mathcal O_C$ is projective in the full
subcategory $\mathcal O_C$, then $Q$ is projective in $\mathcal O$. The proof
is the two adjunction identities
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\operatorname{pr}_CP,X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,X)$
for $X\in\mathcal O_C$ and
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(Q,\operatorname{pr}_CX)$
for general $X\in\mathcal O$, together with exactness of
$\operatorname{pr}_C$; these reduce exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}$ to the
corresponding exactness in $\mathcal O_C$ or in $\mathcal O$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]],
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie
algebra $\mathfrak g$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: a Cartan
subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, a positive system with simple roots $\alpha_i$, the
Weyl group $W$ of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]], the Weyl
vector $\rho$, and the dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$. Write
$Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$ and $\mu\le\lambda$ when
$\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$.

**The fixed weight.** Fix a weight $\lambda$ which is **integral**,
**dot-regular** and **dominant**: $\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z$
for every root $\alpha$ (so the integral Weyl group $W_\lambda$ of
[[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] is all of $W$), and
$\langle\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\neq0$, respectively $>0$, for every
root, respectively every positive root ([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]]).
The set $\Phi_\lambda$ of [[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]] is therefore
the full root system and $W_\lambda=W$.

**The block.** The regular point $\lambda+\rho$ lies in an open chamber. An element fixing
it preserves that chamber, so [[thm-the-weyl-group-acts-simply-transitively-on-weyl-chambers]]
makes its stabilizer trivial; hence the linkage class
$$C=W_\lambda\cdot\lambda=W\cdot\lambda$$
has exactly $|W|$ elements. The **regular integral block** is the full
subcategory
$$\mathcal O_\lambda:=\mathcal O_C$$
of objects of $\mathcal O$ whose simple composition factors have labels in
$C$, as in [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]; it is
nonzero, abelian and extension-closed as a block, and
$K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ is the subgroup of $K_0(\mathcal O)$ of
[[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]] spanned by the classes
of objects of the block.

**Its labelled objects.** For $w\in W$ define the standard and costandard
objects and the simple object by
$$\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=M(w\cdot\lambda),\qquad \nabla(w\cdot\lambda):=D(M(w\cdot\lambda)),\qquad L(w\cdot\lambda):=M(w\cdot\lambda)/J(w\cdot\lambda),$$
where $M$ is the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]], $D$ the restricted dual
of [[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], and $J(w\cdot\lambda)$
the sum of all proper submodules, so that $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ is the unique
simple quotient of $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ by
[[thm-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]. By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ are exactly the $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for
$w\in W$, pairwise non-isomorphic. Let $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ denote a projective
cover of $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, which may be chosen inside the linkage class of
$w\cdot\lambda$ and is unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); every such $P(w\cdot\lambda)$
carries a finite Verma flag
([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]],
[[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]).

**Triangularity of the Verma-flag matrix.** For all $v,w\in W$,
$$[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]\neq0\ \Longrightarrow\ v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda,\qquad [\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=1,$$
where the multiplicity is the composition multiplicity of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]]. Indeed
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]$
by [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] and
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))\neq0$ forces
$w\cdot\lambda-v\cdot\lambda\in Q^+$ while
$(P(v\cdot\lambda):\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))=1$ by
[[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]].

**The antidominant weight.** Let $w_0\in W$ be the longest element. Since
$\langle w_0\cdot\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle
=\langle\lambda+\rho,w_0^{-1}\alpha^\vee\rangle<0$ for every positive root
$\alpha$, the antidominant Verma module $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is simple
([[cor-antidominant-verma-modules-are-simple]]), so
$$\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$
and this is the unique standard object of the block that is simple: for
$w\neq w_0$ the regular weight $w\cdot\lambda$ is not antidominant, so some
positive root $\alpha$ has
$\langle w\cdot\lambda+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, and
[[thm-verma-embedding-for-an-arbitrary-positive-root]] embeds
$M(s_\alpha\cdot(w\cdot\lambda))$ as a proper submodule of
$\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$. The weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ is called the
**antidominant weight** of the block and $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ its
antidominant Verma module.

**Grothendieck group.** By [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]
applied to the finite label set $C=W\cdot\lambda$, both the classes
$[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]$ and the classes $[L(w\cdot\lambda)]$, $w\in W$,
form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$, and the transition matrix
between them is unitriangular for any linear order of $W$ extending the order
on the dot orbit induced by $\le$.

Every statement above uses the published block, Verma, duality and
projective-cover theory named in the citations, and that theory assumes the
Axiom of Choice; the definition itself selects nothing further.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]).

In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the
antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let
$$P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); it is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable ([[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]],
[[def-projective-object]]), and it is an injective object of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is
$$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathbf{mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$
with the left action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M)$ induced by composition on the right of
the source: $a\cdot f=f\circ a$
([[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]). Its
values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are
written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and
$VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$. The functor $V$ is exact, because
$P$ is projective, and hence left exact; the identity
$VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with its regular module structure
is the Yoneda identification. Replacing the chosen projective cover $P$ by an
isomorphic one changes $V$ by a natural equivalence of functors compatible
with the endomorphism-ring identification, so the construction depends only
on the isomorphism class of $P$.

**Well-definedness: $P$ is injective.** We prove that $P$ is an injective
object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ using only the listed suppliers, following the
argument of [Soe90, Sections 1.2 and 2.1] in its algebraic form. Put
$\eta:=-\rho$; then $W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, because $w\cdot\eta=w(\eta+\rho)-\rho=-\rho$
for every $w$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects are the $L(\mu)$ with $L(\mu)$ determined by $\mu$, and the composition
factors of $M(\eta)$ have highest weights in $W\cdot\eta\cap(\eta-Q^+)=\{\eta\}$;
hence $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$ is simple. By BGG reciprocity
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) applied to the single-label block, and the existence
of Verma flags for projectives ([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]),
the projective cover $P(\eta)$ has a Verma flag with the single factor
$\Delta(\eta)=M(\eta)=L(\eta)$, so $P(\eta)\cong L(\eta)$; the block
$\mathcal O_\eta$ has a single simple object, which is projective, hence is
semisimple by enough projectives ([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]),
and therefore every object of $\mathcal O_\eta$, in particular $L(\eta)$, is
injective as well as projective in $\mathcal O_\eta$
([[def-injective-object]]). A projective object of a block is projective in
$\mathcal O$ ([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]), and an
injective object of a block is injective in $\mathcal O$ because the block
decomposition is a direct sum of abelian subcategories and the exact
projections restrict split exactness blockwise. Second, we identify a
projective-injective object
in the block $\mathcal O_\lambda$: let $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$ be the
finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\lambda+\rho$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
and set
$$Q:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\bigl(E\otimes L(\eta)\bigr)\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
the exact central projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]].
Since $L(\eta)$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$, the tensor product
$E\otimes L(\eta)$ is projective and injective
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and its direct summand $Q$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$; the
general exact tensor-block biadjunction of
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] gives the
same conclusion with all adjoints and, by
[[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]],
injectivity (equivalently, $Q$ is a direct summand of a projective-injective
object, and injectivity passes to summands). Third, we compute a
one-dimensional Hom space: since $M(a)$ with $a=w_0\cdot\lambda$ is simple by
the same top-weight argument as for $\eta$ (every other highest weight in
$W\cdot a$ lies strictly above $a$ in the root order), the tensor product
$E^{*}\otimes M(a)$ has a finite Verma flag whose factors are the
$\Delta(a+\nu)$ with $\nu$ running through the weights of the dual module
$E^{*}$, by
[[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]; here
$E^{*}=L(-w_0(\lambda+\rho))$ ([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).
Projecting to the central character $\chi_\eta$ retains exactly the factors
with $a+\nu\in W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, that is $\nu=-w_0(\lambda+\rho)$, the
highest weight of $E^{*}$ of multiplicity one, so
$$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\eta}\bigl(E^{*}\otimes M(a)\bigr)=L(\eta).$$
The tensor-hom adjunction and the tensor-block adjunction now give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,L(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),E^{*}\otimes M(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),L(\eta))\cong\mathbb C,$$
because every homomorphism from the block-$\eta$ simple lands in the
$\chi_\eta$-summand and $L(\eta)$ is simple. Choose the nonzero, hence
surjective, element $q:Q\to L(a)$ and lift it through the projective cover
$P(a)\to L(a)$ to a map $Q\to P(a)$; its image is a submodule of $P(a)$
surjecting onto the head $L(a)$, hence is all of $P(a)$ by essentiality of a
projective cover, so the lift is surjective and splits by projectivity of
$P(a)$. Therefore $P(a)$ is a direct summand of the injective object $Q$
([[def-injective-object]]), and direct summands of injective objects are
injective, so $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is injective. This argument uses
[[thm-bgg-verma-homomorphism-criterion]] only through the standard embedding
criterion implicit in the top-weight computations, and it does not assume the
Endomorphismensatz.

**The once-each flag.** The tensor flag of $E\otimes M(-\rho)$ has labels
$-\rho+\gamma$ for weights $\gamma$ of $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$. Projection to
$\chi_\lambda$ keeps precisely $\gamma\in W(\lambda+\rho)$, each of
multiplicity one by [[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]].
Thus $Q$ has each $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ once. Every such Verma contains
$M(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(a)$ by
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]]. BGG
reciprocity gives $(P(a):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))\ge1$; the splitting
$Q=P(a)\oplus Q'$ and
[[lem-direct-summands-of-verma-filtered-objects-are-verma-filtered]] give the
opposite bound one. Hence all these multiplicities equal one, $Q'$ has
an empty flag and is zero, and $Q=P(a)$. Since $P(a)$ is projective,
$V$ is exact and $\dim VX=[X:L(a)]$ for finite-length $X$: on simples its
values are $\mathbb C$ at the head label and zero otherwise. Consequently
$\dim V\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)=1$ for every $x$. Every simple submodule of a
Verma is itself a simple Verma: its universal Verma map into that Verma is
injective. Thus the unique simple standard $L(a)$ is its only possible
socle label, and [[thm-verma-homomorphism-spaces-have-dimension-at-most-one]]
makes this socle a single copy of $L(a)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of
the Cartan subalgebra of [[def-bgg-category-o]], graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$
as fixed on this page ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]],
[[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]). Let
$\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$
by
$$x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1\quad(x\in\mathfrak h),\qquad x\cdot(s\otimes1)=0\quad(x\in\mathfrak n^+),$$
where for $x\in\mathfrak h$, $xs$ means multiplication by the
linear polynomial $x\in S(\mathfrak h)$; $\mathfrak n^+$ acts trivially. Put
$$M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U(\mathfrak b)}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda),$$
a module over $\mathfrak g\otimes S$: the left $\mathfrak g$-action is induced,
and $S$ acts on the right by multiplication on the last factor, which commutes
with $\mathfrak g$. Specializing at a closed point $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$ gives
$$M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon),$$
the Verma module of [[def-verma-module]]; this is the universal family of
Verma modules with deformation parameter $\epsilon$.

**The family.** For a localization $T$ of $S$ put
$M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$, and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the
full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of
a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional
$\mathfrak g$-modules $E$. Write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for
$R=S_{(0)}$, the localization of $S$ at the origin of
$\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment
$T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors
$-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of
$\operatorname{Spec} T$. By the tensor identity for finite-dimensional modules
and the Verma flags of tensor products
([[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]) the
specializations have Verma constituents of highest weights
$\lambda+\nu+\epsilon$, where $\nu$ runs through the weights of the
finite-dimensional tensor factors, and they can meet several
central-character blocks, whose labels are the dot-Weyl orbits through these
highest weights ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]); a generic
parameter is generally nonintegral, and the distinct constituent labels have distinct central characters at the
generic parameter: an equality $\lambda+\gamma+\tau+\rho=w(\lambda+\gamma'+\tau+\rho)$
as affine functions of $\tau$ forces $w=1$ by comparing linear parts,
and then $\gamma=\gamma'$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]).

**Selected components.** For a regular dominant integral source $\lambda$ as in
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] and a
dot-dominant integral target $\nu$, so that $\nu+\rho$ lies in the closed
positive chamber, denote by $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ the component of
$\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ whose closed fiber at the origin lies in the selected
target block $\mathcal O_\nu$ of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. Finite Verma flags of the
deformed tensor products and pairwise-unit resultants of their
central-character polynomials define this component by actual central
idempotents over $R$, obtained from [[thm-chinese-remainder-theorem-for-comaximal-ideals]].
Indeed choose a linear combination $z$ of central elements separating the
finitely many distinct special characters. On each deformed Verma factor,
$z$ acts by a polynomial $c_i(\tau)$ by
[[lem-harish-chandra-projection-computes-highest-weight-scalars]], and a flag
is annihilated by $\prod_i(z-c_i(\tau))$. Group these factors by their
constant values at the origin; differences from different groups are units
in $R$, so their product polynomials are comaximal in $R[X]$. CRT gives
mutually orthogonal polynomial projectors, whose images are the selected
components and whose sum is the identity. Other central-character components remain part of the full tensor
family; thus whole-family statements and selected-block statements are
distinguished.

**Weight structure.** Write $\tau:\mathfrak h\to T$ for the tautological linear map.
Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry a **deformed weight decomposition**
$X=\bigoplus_\xi X^\xi$, where
$$X^\xi=\{m:(h-\tau(h))m=\xi(h)m\text{ for every }h\in\mathfrak h\}.$$
These are eigenmodules for $h-\tau(h)$, not ordinary complex weight spaces
for $h$. They are finite projective, hence locally free of finite rank over $T$, as follows from the PBW model of Verma modules and the
flatness of the localization
([[thm-pbw-ordered-monomial-basis-for-the-enveloping-algebra]]). The
conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1]; no choice beyond the inherited
Axiom of Choice of the block theory is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$ the localization at the origin, and use the selected
component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed
family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]]. For
every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed
$\lambda$-block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to
isomorphism, and every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one
of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same
multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this
block is a direct summand of a finite sum of truncated induced projectives
representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras
$R\to R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category
and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_RR'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_RR',N\otimes_RR').$$
For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$ this Hom module is finite free over
local $R$. A $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map between such finite
projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is
itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target
$\nu$, including singular $\nu$, the same local projective construction gives
all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_\nu$;
these lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ of a
regular-source tensor family. It is neither necessary nor asserted that the
singular Verma itself generates every target projective, and the other central
components of the full tensor family are not claimed to have only these
indecomposables.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of
[[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a
localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$:

1. The canonical map
$$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_ZT\longrightarrow\bigl(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\bigr)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\bigl(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\bigr),$$
is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and the center $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ ([[thm-harish-chandra-isomorphism-for-the-center]]) followed by evaluation at $\lambda+\rho+\epsilon$ on the universal parameter $\epsilon$.
2. For finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E,F$, the $T$-module
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$
is free of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^{*})_0$, and the natural base-change map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\kappa(\epsilon)}(M\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon),N\otimes_T\kappa(\epsilon))$$
is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec}T$.
3. $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$.
4. If a $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism.

Let $k$ be a field and let $r\ge0$ be an integer. Then $k[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is a
unique factorisation domain ([[def-unique-factorisation-domain]]). Every
irreducible element of it is prime
([[def-irreducible-and-prime-elements-in-a-domain]]), and every prime ideal of
height one ([[def-height-of-a-prime-ideal]]) is generated by an irreducible
element.

For $r=0$ the ring is the field $k$ itself
([[def-multivariate-polynomial-ring-by-iteration]]); it has no irreducibles and
no height-one primes.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group acting faithfully on its $r$-dimensional complex reflection representation $V$, and put $S=\mathbb C[V]$. Then $S^W$ is a polynomial algebra on $r$ homogeneous algebraically independent basic invariants, and $S$ is free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$. More generally these conclusions hold for every finite subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}(V)$ generated by complex reflections (nonidentity transformations fixing a hyperplane pointwise). In the Weyl case the generating root reflections have order two; no classification or Coxeter presentation is needed here.

Orbit sums indexed by the distinct $W$-orbits in $P$ form a complex vector-space basis of $\mathbb C[P]^W$. Equivalently they are indexed by dominant integral weights, with exactly one per orbit, including weights on chamber walls. Every invariant has finite support in this basis.

For each dominant $\lambda$, the set of dominant $\mu\le\lambda$ is finite. In fact every such $\mu$ satisfies $\|\mu\|\le\|\lambda\|$ for the specified invariant Euclidean norm. All assertions are choice-free.

Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the cited invariant-theory results
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with
Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$, acting on $\mathfrak h^*$
by the root reflections of [[def-root-reflections-and-the-weyl-group-action]]
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]]), hence on the
symmetric algebra $S=S(\mathfrak h^*)$ by graded algebra automorphisms; a nondegenerate $W$-invariant bilinear form identifies $\mathfrak h$
with $\mathfrak h^*$ and thus identifies $S$ with $S(\mathfrak h)$ as
a graded $W$-algebra. Such a form is the complexification of a positive
definite form on the real Cartan, obtained by averaging any positive
definite form over finite $W$. Fix this identification; the page writes
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$ for either presentation. Write
$$S^W_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}(S^W)_d,\qquad I:=S\,S^W_+,$$
so that $I$ is the homogeneous ideal of $S$ generated by the invariants of
positive degree; this is the specialization to the reflection group case of
the quotient construction of
[[def-finite-linear-invariant-and-coinvariant-polynomial-algebras]], because
$S^W_+$ is exactly the space of positive-degree elements of the invariant
algebra $S^W$.

The **coinvariant algebra** of the pair $(\mathfrak h,W)$ is the graded
quotient
$$C=C(\mathfrak h,W):=S/I.$$
It is a commutative graded $\mathbb C$-algebra with $C_0=\mathbb C$: the ideal
$I$ is homogeneous of positive degree, so constants survive and every
homogeneous piece of $S$ maps onto its image. The quotient map
$$\rho:S\longrightarrow C,\qquad \rho(f)=f+I,$$
is a surjective graded algebra homomorphism, and the action of $W$ on $S$
descends to a $\mathbb C$-linear action on $C$ by graded algebra
automorphisms, because $I$ is $W$-stable. The algebra $C$ is finite
dimensional: $W$ is generated by its root reflections, so
[[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]] writes $S$ as a free
module of finite rank over the polynomial algebra $S^W$, and
[[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]] gives
$\dim_{\mathbb C}C=|W|<\infty$ with the graded Hilbert series recorded there.

**Degree normalization.** Throughout the Soergel material on this page the
Cartan generators are given degree $2$, that is $\deg\mathfrak h=2$; the
symmetric algebra $S$ is then graded with $\deg S_d=2d$ for homogeneous
polynomials of ordinary degree $d$, and $C$ inherits this doubled grading. In
particular a basic invariant of ordinary degree $d_i$ has page degree $2d_i$,
and the top nonzero degree of $C$ is $2N$ with
$N=\sum_i(d_i-1)$. The separate degree-sum lemma on this page proves
that this number equals the positive-root count.

**Auxiliary permutation model for type $A$.** For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_n$
one may instead work with the place-permuting $S_n$-action on the auxiliary
polynomial ring $S_{\mathrm{perm}}=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, where a
permutation $\sigma$ sends $x_i$ to $x_{\sigma(i)}$, and with the quotient
$$C_{\mathrm{perm}}:=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n),$$
where $e_1,\dots,e_n$ are the elementary symmetric polynomials. Splitting the
permutation representation $\mathbb C^n=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathbb C\cdot(1,\dots,1)$
into its sum-zero Cartan part and its fixed average coordinate exhibits
$\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]\cong S(\mathfrak h)\otimes\mathbb C[e_1]$ with
$e_1=x_1+\cdots+x_n$ the invariant coordinate, and restriction to the hyperplane
$e_1=0$ has kernel $(e_1)$. By [[thm-fundamental-theorem-of-symmetric-polynomials]], $e_1,\dots,e_n$
generate the invariant algebra and its positive-degree ideal of the permutation action, while $e_2,\dots,e_n$ restrict to basic
invariants of $S(\mathfrak h)^W$, dividing out by the positive-degree invariants
commutes with this presentation and yields a canonical isomorphism of graded
algebras
$$C(\mathfrak h,W)\cong C_{\mathrm{perm}}=\mathbb C[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n),$$
in which $x_i$ has degree $2$ and $e_i$ has degree $2i$. Elements of $C$ are
written as classes $\rho(f)$; the auxiliary model is used only for explicit
rank computations and never replaces the intrinsic definition.

The quotient and finite coordinate constructions require no additional choice;
the freeness and Hilbert-series conclusions inherit AC from their suppliers.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory
items. Let $W$ act on the Cartan space $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra
$C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then there
is a $W$-stable graded subspace $\mathcal H\subseteq S$, finite dimensional of
dimension $|W|$, such that the multiplication map
$$S^W\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S,\qquad p\otimes h\mapsto ph,$$
is an isomorphism of graded $S^W$-modules and of $W$-modules, and the
restriction of the quotient map $\rho:S\to C$ to $\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism
of graded $W$-modules $\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C$. One may take
$$\mathcal H=\{f\in S:\partial_pf=0\text{ for all }p\in S^W_+\},$$
using constant-coefficient differential operators from a $W$-invariant
positive definite form on $\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}$. Any $W$-stable graded
complement of $I$ has the same multiplication and quotient properties. This
is the simultaneous kernel of all positive-degree invariant differential
operators, not in general the kernel of the quadratic Laplacian alone. In particular $\dim\mathcal H_d=\dim C_d$ for every $d$ and
$\sum_d\dim\mathcal H_d=|W|$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory
items. Let $W$ act on the Cartan space $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra
$C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Let
$w_1,\dots,w_r$ be homogeneous basic invariants of page degrees
$2d_1,\dots,2d_r$, where $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical degrees
($\deg\mathfrak h=1$; for the Cartan of $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ they are
$2,3,\dots,n$), so that $S^W=\mathbb C[w_1,\dots,w_r]$
([[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]]), and let
$\rho:S\to C$ be the quotient by the ideal $I=(w_1,\dots,w_r)$. Put
$N:=\sum_{i=1}^r(d_i-1)$. Then:

1. The sequence $w_1,\dots,w_r$ is a homogeneous $S$-regular sequence and $C$
is a complete intersection: $C=S/(w_1,\dots,w_r)$ with
$$\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t)=\frac{\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})}{(1-t^2)^r}=\prod_i(1+t^2+\cdots+t^{2(d_i-1)}),$$
so that $\dim_{\mathbb C}C_{2N}=1$ and $C_j=0$ for $j>2N$.
2. The multiplication pairing $C_i\times C_{2N-i}\to C_{2N}\cong\mathbb C$ is
nondegenerate for every $i$, and consequently
$$\operatorname{soc}(C)=\{c\in C:C_+c=0\}=C_{2N}$$ is one dimensional.
3. Equivalently, $C$ is a graded Gorenstein algebra with one-dimensional socle
in the top degree $2N$.

derivations.claim: The block at $\eta=-\rho$ has a single highest weight in $W\cdot\eta\cap(\eta-Q^+)=\{\eta\}$, so $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$ is simple, its projective cover has a Verma flag whose single factor is $L(\eta)$ by BGG reciprocity, hence equals $L(\eta)$ and $L(\eta)$ is projective; with a single simple object and enough projectives the block is semisimple, so $L(\eta)$ is injective as well, and the well-definedness part of [F6] then supplies the object $Q=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}(E\otimes L(\eta))$, which is projective and injective and has a Verma flag with the factors $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$, $x\in W$, once each, together with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,L(a))\cong\mathbb C$ and a split embedding $P(a)\hookrightarrow Q$; the same construction with the distinct extremal weights $Wv=W/W_\nu$ gives the singular once-each flag.

Let $p$ be a height-one prime of $R$, $T=R_p$, $k=\operatorname{Frac}(R/p)$, and let $\tau$ be the tautological parameter of the deformed family; the residual central characters are the $W$-classes of the points $xv+\tau$, $x\in W$, and $\chi_{xv+\tau}=\chi_{yv+\tau}$ over $k$ forces $xv+\tau=w(yv+\tau)$ for some $w$ by [F1] and finite interpolation, so comparing the constant and linear parts modulo $p$ gives $xv=wyv$ and $w\tau=\tau$ in $k$; a nonidentity $w$ fixing the generic point of the divisor $p$ fixes a hyperplane, hence is the orthogonal reflection in that hyperplane. That hyperplane must be a root hyperplane: otherwise it contains a root-regular real point, whose open chamber would be stabilized by $w$, contradicting [[thm-the-weyl-group-acts-simply-transitively-on-weyl-chambers]]. Thus $p$ is the root prime $\langle\tau,\alpha^\vee\rangle$ for that root; therefore at every nonroot prime all residual characters are pairwise distinct, while at the root prime the equal-character classes are exactly the pairs $\{x,s_\alpha x\}$ together with singleton classes wherever $s_\alpha xv=xv$, which occurs in the singular case.

At a root divisor, isolate one two-element residual character class by CRT. Write its upper and lower weights $A=a+\tau$ and $B=b+\tau$, where $b=s_\alpha\cdot a=a-n\alpha$ and $n=\langle a+\rho,\alpha^\vee\rangle>0$. Over $k=\operatorname{Frac}(R/p)$, a singular vector of weight $A-\gamma$ must satisfy the Casimir equation $2(A+\rho,\gamma)=(\gamma,\gamma)$. Its parameter term vanishes identically on the divisor only if $\gamma$ is a multiple of $\alpha$, and its constant term then forces $\gamma=n\alpha$. The Shapovalov determinant on that weight has valuation one: only its $(\alpha,n)$ factor vanishes, with exponent $K(0)=1$, so its residue radical has dimension one there. A nonzero radical has a highest-weight vector, by choosing minimal root height among its nonzero weight spaces; it is therefore generated initially by that one-dimensional $B$-weight space. The same Casimir equation for $B$ has no solution with positive $\gamma$, so $M(B)$ is simple. Its highest vector gives an injected $M(B)\to M(A)$: the induced map is injective because its simple source is nonzero. Any nonzero quotient of the radical by this image would again have a highest-weight vector; the equation forces weight $B$, but its $B$-space is zero. Thus $\operatorname{Rad}M(A)=M(B)$ and $M(A)$ has length two. This proves the required divisor-field classification directly; no closed-point or complex-only classification is substituted for it.

Let $u=\nu+\rho$ be dominant with $H=\operatorname{Stab}(u)$, and $v=\lambda+\rho$ regular dominant. For onto translation, a retained factor satisfies $yv+\gamma=xu$. The norm bound and dominant-distance inequality force equality $|\gamma|=|u-v|$ and $x^{-1}yv\in Hv$; because $v$ is regular this means $x^{-1}y\in H$, hence $xu=yu$. Thus the retained standard is $\Delta(y\cdot\nu)$ once. This uses the coset condition, not the false assertion $Hv=\{v\}$. For return translation the retained labels are $x\in yH$, each extremal weight once. The conclusion is a Verma flag with factors $\Delta(yh\cdot\lambda)$ for $h\in H$, not a direct sum. The same calculation applies to the deformed tensor flags, with the common parameter $\tau$ retained.

Every standard $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ contains $L(a)$ as a composition factor: $a$ is the minimal weight of $W\cdot a$, so the Verma embedding criterion gives a nonzero, hence injective, map $M(a)=L(a)\to\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$, and BGG reciprocity gives $(P(a):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(x\cdot\lambda):L(a)]\ge1$, while $(P(a):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))\le(Q:\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))=1$ because $P(a)$ is a summand of $Q$; hence all multiplicities equal one, the complementary summand of $P(a)$ in $Q$ has flag length zero, and $Q=P(a)$; the argument applies verbatim to a dot-dominant singular $\nu$ with $Wv$ replaced by $W/W_\nu$.

Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $B=R\otimes_{R^W}R$. Localization of the free invariant/harmonic decomposition in [F8] makes it finite free of rank $|W|$ over the right $R$. Evaluation embeds it into $K^W$ by $f\otimes r\mapsto(f(x^{-1}\tau)r)_x$: generically the orbit has $|W|$ distinct points, interpolation makes this map surjective after tensoring with $K$, and freeness makes it injective over $R$. At a nonroot height-one prime, residual orbit points are distinct and CRT gives $B_T=T^W$. At a root prime CRT isolates the pairs from step 1.2. Every pair evaluation is congruent modulo the root uniformizer $\alpha=\langle\tau,\alpha^\vee\rangle$. Choose a linear $f$ for which the two values differ by a unit times $\alpha$; subtract its lower value and multiply by the pair projector to obtain $(\alpha,0)$. Together with the pair identity this generates exactly the congruence order $\{(u,v)\in T^2:u-v\in\alpha T\}$. For a singular stabilizer $H=W_\nu$, Reynolds averaging on the first factor identifies $B^H=R^H\otimes_{R^W}R$. It is finite projective over right $R$ as a split summand of $B$, hence free since $R$ is local; its generic rank is $|W/H|$. The same pair and singleton orders, now on cosets, follow by taking the $H$-fixed tuples.

Localize $P_R$ to $T=R_p$. Its full flag still has $|W|$ factors; CRT in the finitely many residual central characters splits it into pair components and singleton components. Write $P_{T,\{A,B\}}$ for one pair summand. Only this summand has the two factors $\Delta_T(A)$ and $\Delta_T(B)$ once. Maximal-weight generation gives $0\to\Delta_T(A)\to P_{T,\{A,B\}}\to\Delta_T(B)\to0$. It is projective in its character component by base change and splitting. The residual extension cannot split: otherwise its direct summand $M(B)$ would be projective, but duality applied to the nonsplit length-two $M(A)$ yields a nonsplit extension $0\to L(A)\to D M(A)\to L(B)=M(B)\to0$, contradicting projectivity. At a singleton the summand has a single standard. The identical argument applies to the singular once-each flag, with root-fixed labels giving singletons. Over the fraction field all standard characters are distinct and all Vermas are simple by the Shapovalov determinant; hence each component is its indicated standard and the generic endomorphism algebra is the tuple algebra.

Translation out carries $P_R^\nu$ to a regular projective by the exact tensor biadjunction and the actual central projectors. Its flag contains every regular standard once by steps 2.1 and 1.4. On the closed fiber, onto translation takes the regular antidominant simple Verma to the singular antidominant simple Verma, so adjunction gives a one-dimensional Hom from the return projective to the regular antidominant simple. Its regular antidominant cover splits off; both have every standard once, so the complement has zero flag and vanishes. Hom base change and the two-map lifting argument of [F7] now give $T_{\mathrm{out}}P_R^\nu\cong P_R^\lambda$. Any two choices induce the same endomorphism map after identification, since the endomorphism algebra is commutative (as will follow from its generic tuple embedding).

Any endomorphism $f$ of the isolated pair $P_{T,\{A,B\}}$ preserves $\Delta_T(A)$ and acts by scalars $u_a$ on $\Delta_T(A)$ and $u_b$ on $\Delta_T(B)$; if $u_a-u_b$ were a unit modulo $p$, the residual projector $(f-u_b)/(u_a-u_b)$, polynomial in $f$ since $(f-u_a)(f-u_b)=0$ on the two-step flag, would split the nonsplit residual extension of step 3.1, so $u_a\equiv u_b$ modulo $\tau(\alpha^\vee)$ and $\operatorname{End}(P_{T,\{A,B\}})$ lies in the congruence order; the central Casimir element acts on the two generic standards by $(A,A+2\rho)$ and $(B,B+2\rho)$, eigenvalues differing by $2n(\alpha,\tau)=n(\alpha,\alpha)\langle\tau,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, a unit times the uniformizer, so the Casimir minus the lower eigenvalue gives the pair $(\tau(\alpha^\vee),0)$ and together with the identity generates the full congruence order, both generators being central actions; on singleton classes the order is $T$, generated by the identity.

The generic tuple embeddings place $\operatorname{End}(P_R)$ and $B$ (or $\operatorname{End}(P_R^\nu)$ and $B^H$) inside the same tuple algebra. Both are finite free right-$R$ modules: for End this is [F7], for $B^H$ it is Reynolds averaging in step 2.2. Steps 3.1, 2.2 and 4.1 identify their localizations at each height-one prime, pair by pair, including the singular singletons. A finite free $R$-lattice equals the intersection of its height-one localizations inside its fraction-field span. Indeed $R$ is a localization of a polynomial UFD, and $R=\bigcap_{\operatorname{ht}p=1}R_p$: a reduced fractional denominator outside $R$ has a nonunit irreducible factor detected at its prime; applying this coefficientwise to any free lattice basis proves the lattice assertion. Thus the two lattices are equal and yield the asserted algebra identification. This does not yet assert that the global central image is saturated; its surjectivity is established separately below.

For a dominant shifted weight $u$ with stabilizer $H$, the closed right fiber of $B^H$ is $C^H$, because averaging commutes with quotienting by the right maximal ideal. Choose $N$ above the largest ordinary polynomial degree in $C$, and choose an $H$-invariant representative $h(\tau)$ of any prescribed class in $C^H$ by averaging. Prescribe the jet $h(X-u)$ of order $N$ at $u$, and zero jets at the other distinct points in $Wu$. Polynomial CRT produces $q$ with those jets. Then $p(X)=|H|^{-1}\sum_{w\in W}q(w^{-1}X)$ is $W$-invariant. At $X=u+\tau$, precisely the $w\in H$ terms contribute, and their jets equal $h(w^{-1}\tau)=h(\tau)$; the other terms vanish to order $N$. Hence $p(u+\tau)\equiv h(\tau)\pmod{(\tau)^N}$, whose image in $C$ is the prescribed class. In the regular case take $u=v$ and $H=1$; in the singular case take the actual singular $u$, never regular $v$. By [F1], $p=\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)$ for a central element $z$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the
regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] the
assignment
$$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]\longmapsto w,$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and for every simple reflection $s$ the
wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies
$$c\,[\theta_sX]=c\,[X]\cdot(1+s)\qquad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
right multiplication by $1+s$ in the integral group ring $\mathbb Z[W]$.
Consequently, for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$ one has
$$c\,[\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s_1)(1+s_2)\cdots(1+s_k),$$
the sum of all subexpression products with their actual multiplicities; its top
Bruhat term is $w$ once and all other terms have strictly smaller labels. With
the composition $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$ instead, the factors are
multiplied in the reverse order.

Assume the Axiom of Choice.

Fix a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$, and a positive Borel $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$. Write $Q^+=\sum_i\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\alpha_i$, $\mu\leq\lambda$ when $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$, and $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+\rho)-\rho$.

The classes $[L(\lambda)]$, and separately the classes $[M(\lambda)]$, form $\mathbb Z$-bases of $K_0(\mathcal O)$. For a fixed finite central-character label set $\Lambda=W\cdot\lambda$, the transition between its standard and simple classes is unitriangular in any linear order extending $\leq$. This remains true on a downward-closed subset of that finite poset. It is not a claim about finite downward ideals of all of $\mathfrak h^*$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Work in category
$\mathcal O$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]], and write
$\Delta(\mu)=M(\mu)$ for the standard objects of
[[def-standard-and-costandard-objects-in-category-o]], i.e. the Verma modules
of [[def-verma-module]].

A **finite Verma flag** of an object $X$ of $\mathcal O$ — also called a
**standard flag** or a **$\Delta$-flag** — is a finite increasing sequence of
subobjects
$$0=X_0\subseteq X_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq X_n=X$$
such that each quotient $X_i/X_{i-1}$ is isomorphic to a Verma module
$\Delta(\mu_i)=M(\mu_i)$, for $i=1,\dots,n$. An object admitting such a flag is
called **Verma-filtered**. Since the flag is exhausted by its factors, its
class in the Grothendieck group
$K_0(\mathcal O)$ of [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]]
is
$$[X]=\sum_{i=1}^n[\Delta(\mu_i)].$$

For a Verma-filtered object $X$ and a weight $\mu$, the **multiplicity**
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is the number of indices $i$ with $\mu_i=\mu$ in a Verma
flag of $X$. This number is independent of the chosen flag by
[[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], so the notation
$(X:\Delta(\mu))$ is well-defined for Verma-filtered $X$.

The zero object has the empty flag, and every multiplicity of the zero object
is zero; a nonzero Verma-filtered object has at least one factor. A one-step
flag of $X$ is exactly an isomorphism $X\cong\Delta(\mu)$ for a single weight
$\mu$, so the objects with a one-step flag are the Verma modules themselves.
The flag is a chain of subobjects of $X$ in the module category; it is not
required to split, and later examples show that it need not.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral block with dominant
representative $\lambda$:

1. Projective functors form a Krull-Schmidt category.
2. Their indecomposables are indexed by $W$, with $\Theta_w$ characterized by
$\Theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$. For a reduced word
$w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the functor $\Theta_w$ is a multiplicity-one summand of
$\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, and every other indecomposable summand has a
label $x<w$. In particular every indecomposable projective functor is generated
as a summand by wall crossings.
3. Two projective functors are naturally equivalent exactly when their induced
operators on the Grothendieck group agree.

The characterization concerns evaluation on the dominant projective Verma; no
faithfulness of that evaluation on all natural maps of arbitrary
endofunctors is asserted.

derivations.claim: The two class computations are $c[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s)(1+t)=1+s+t+st$ and $c[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+t)(1+s)=1+t+s+ts$, that is $[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)]=[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(st\cdot\lambda)]$ and $[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)]=[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ts\cdot\lambda)]$.

The two products of [F1], $(1+s)(1+t)$ and $(1+t)(1+s)$, differ: the coefficient of the length-two element $st$ is one in the first and zero in the second, and vice versa for $ts$, while $st\ne ts$ in $S_3$ and the standard classes form a $\mathbb Z$-basis, so the induced class operators on $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ are different and already differ on the single class $[\Delta(\lambda)]$.
By the determination theorem, two projective functors whose class operators on $K_0$ differ are not naturally equivalent; hence $\theta_s\theta_t\not\cong\theta_t\theta_s$.

Feeding one factor at a time gives $c[\theta_s^2X]=c[X](1+s)^2=2c[X](1+s)=2c[\theta_sX]$ for every $X$, so the class operators of $\theta_s^2$ and of $\theta_s\oplus\theta_s$ agree and the determination theorem gives $\theta_s^2\cong\theta_s\oplus\theta_s\not\cong\operatorname{id}$, since $\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)$ has nonzero class $1+s$; hence $s\mapsto\theta_s$ is not a representation of $W$, the wall-crossing classes are the specialized self-dual Hecke generators $1+s$, whose square is $2(1+s)$; the group generator is recovered on classes by $s=[\theta_s]-1$, and 'generated by wall-crossing' cannot be read as the assignment $s\mapsto\theta_s$ being a representation of $W$.
