citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed
antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S^W$
for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
$\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+\rho+\epsilon)$, and define
$$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))\otimes r.$$
Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$
are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra
isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$
On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$
acts by the scalar
$\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(x(\lambda+\rho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$;
these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on
$P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the
endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant
integral $\nu$ the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where
$W_\nu$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the
singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted
Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion
$R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$ the localization at the origin, and use the selected
component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed
family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]]. For
every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed
$\lambda$-block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to
isomorphism, and every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one
of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same
multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this
block is a direct summand of a finite sum of truncated induced projectives
representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras
$R\to R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category
and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_RR'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_RR',N\otimes_RR').$$
For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$ this Hom module is finite free over
local $R$. A $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map between such finite
projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is
itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target
$\nu$, including singular $\nu$, the same local projective construction gives
all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_\nu$;
these lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ of a
regular-source tensor family. It is neither necessary nor asserted that the
singular Verma itself generates every target projective, and the other central
components of the full tensor family are not claimed to have only these
indecomposables.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex
semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block
and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$.
Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan
reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then:

(1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention,
followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
(multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel;

(2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$
identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective,
canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its
isomorphism class;

(3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the
coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or
used.

This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral
case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the
invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]).

In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the
antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let
$$P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); it is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable ([[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]],
[[def-projective-object]]), and it is an injective object of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is
$$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathbf{mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$
with the left action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M)$ induced by composition on the right of
the source: $a\cdot f=f\circ a$
([[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]). Its
values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are
written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and
$VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$. The functor $V$ is exact, because
$P$ is projective, and hence left exact; the identity
$VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with its regular module structure
is the Yoneda identification. Replacing the chosen projective cover $P$ by an
isomorphic one changes $V$ by a natural equivalence of functors compatible
with the endomorphism-ring identification, so the construction depends only
on the isomorphism class of $P$.

**Well-definedness: $P$ is injective.** We prove that $P$ is an injective
object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ using only the listed suppliers, following the
argument of [Soe90, Sections 1.2 and 2.1] in its algebraic form. Put
$\eta:=-\rho$; then $W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, because $w\cdot\eta=w(\eta+\rho)-\rho=-\rho$
for every $w$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects are the $L(\mu)$ with $L(\mu)$ determined by $\mu$, and the composition
factors of $M(\eta)$ have highest weights in $W\cdot\eta\cap(\eta-Q^+)=\{\eta\}$;
hence $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$ is simple. By BGG reciprocity
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) applied to the single-label block, and the existence
of Verma flags for projectives ([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]),
the projective cover $P(\eta)$ has a Verma flag with the single factor
$\Delta(\eta)=M(\eta)=L(\eta)$, so $P(\eta)\cong L(\eta)$; the block
$\mathcal O_\eta$ has a single simple object, which is projective, hence is
semisimple by enough projectives ([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]),
and therefore every object of $\mathcal O_\eta$, in particular $L(\eta)$, is
injective as well as projective in $\mathcal O_\eta$
([[def-injective-object]]). A projective object of a block is projective in
$\mathcal O$ ([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]), and an
injective object of a block is injective in $\mathcal O$ because the block
decomposition is a direct sum of abelian subcategories and the exact
projections restrict split exactness blockwise. Second, we identify a
projective-injective object
in the block $\mathcal O_\lambda$: let $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$ be the
finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\lambda+\rho$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
and set
$$Q:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\bigl(E\otimes L(\eta)\bigr)\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
the exact central projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]].
Since $L(\eta)$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$, the tensor product
$E\otimes L(\eta)$ is projective and injective
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and its direct summand $Q$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$; the
general exact tensor-block biadjunction of
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] gives the
same conclusion with all adjoints and, by
[[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]],
injectivity (equivalently, $Q$ is a direct summand of a projective-injective
object, and injectivity passes to summands). Third, we compute a
one-dimensional Hom space: since $M(a)$ with $a=w_0\cdot\lambda$ is simple by
the same top-weight argument as for $\eta$ (every other highest weight in
$W\cdot a$ lies strictly above $a$ in the root order), the tensor product
$E^{*}\otimes M(a)$ has a finite Verma flag whose factors are the
$\Delta(a+\nu)$ with $\nu$ running through the weights of the dual module
$E^{*}$, by
[[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]; here
$E^{*}=L(-w_0(\lambda+\rho))$ ([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).
Projecting to the central character $\chi_\eta$ retains exactly the factors
with $a+\nu\in W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, that is $\nu=-w_0(\lambda+\rho)$, the
highest weight of $E^{*}$ of multiplicity one, so
$$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\eta}\bigl(E^{*}\otimes M(a)\bigr)=L(\eta).$$
The tensor-hom adjunction and the tensor-block adjunction now give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,L(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),E^{*}\otimes M(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),L(\eta))\cong\mathbb C,$$
because every homomorphism from the block-$\eta$ simple lands in the
$\chi_\eta$-summand and $L(\eta)$ is simple. Choose the nonzero, hence
surjective, element $q:Q\to L(a)$ and lift it through the projective cover
$P(a)\to L(a)$ to a map $Q\to P(a)$; its image is a submodule of $P(a)$
surjecting onto the head $L(a)$, hence is all of $P(a)$ by essentiality of a
projective cover, so the lift is surjective and splits by projectivity of
$P(a)$. Therefore $P(a)$ is a direct summand of the injective object $Q$
([[def-injective-object]]), and direct summands of injective objects are
injective, so $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is injective. This argument uses
[[thm-bgg-verma-homomorphism-criterion]] only through the standard embedding
criterion implicit in the top-weight computations, and it does not assume the
Endomorphismensatz.

**The once-each flag.** The tensor flag of $E\otimes M(-\rho)$ has labels
$-\rho+\gamma$ for weights $\gamma$ of $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$. Projection to
$\chi_\lambda$ keeps precisely $\gamma\in W(\lambda+\rho)$, each of
multiplicity one by [[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]].
Thus $Q$ has each $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ once. Every such Verma contains
$M(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(a)$ by
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]]. BGG
reciprocity gives $(P(a):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))\ge1$; the splitting
$Q=P(a)\oplus Q'$ and
[[lem-direct-summands-of-verma-filtered-objects-are-verma-filtered]] give the
opposite bound one. Hence all these multiplicities equal one, $Q'$ has
an empty flag and is zero, and $Q=P(a)$. Since $P(a)$ is projective,
$V$ is exact and $\dim VX=[X:L(a)]$ for finite-length $X$: on simples its
values are $\mathbb C$ at the head label and zero otherwise. Consequently
$\dim V\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)=1$ for every $x$. Every simple submodule of a
Verma is itself a simple Verma: its universal Verma map into that Verma is
injective. Thus the unique simple standard $L(a)$ is its only possible
socle label, and [[thm-verma-homomorphism-spaces-have-dimension-at-most-one]]
makes this socle a single copy of $L(a)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block
with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor
$V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant
algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]],
so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$
and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map
$$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$
is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of
objects killed by $V$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ the
translation functor $T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]) is exact, and
$T_{\chi',E^*,\chi}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of
$T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$; in particular both functors send projectives to
projectives and injectives to injectives. Consequently, in the setting of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], $T_\mu^\lambda$ is both a left
and a right adjoint of $T_\lambda^\mu$, and the two functors are exact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let
$\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection
$s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the
object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two
factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with
multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group
$$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$
Moreover $\theta_s$ is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects with finite
Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities
$(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_sX$ has one with multiplicities
$(\theta_sX:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$,
and the same formula holds in $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$. The resulting flag is
not in general split; splitting is neither asserted nor used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block and
translation theory ([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]).

Fix the dominant regular integral representative $\lambda$ of a regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]) and an
integral weight $\mu$ such that $\lambda+\rho$ is regular dominant and
$\mu+\rho$ is dominant with dot stabilizer exactly $\{1,s\}$ for a reflection
$s=s_\alpha$; this is the dominant-chamber version of single-wall translation
data, the published
[[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] being stated with
antidominant representatives, and the dominant standard counts below are
proved through the norm-distance and extremal-weight bounds
([[lem-dominant-norm-distance-comparison]],
[[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]]) rather than
by applying that datum literally. Let $\nu$ be the unique dominant element of
the linear Weyl orbit of $\mu-\lambda$ and let
$E=L(\nu)$ be the finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\nu$, so
that $\mu-\lambda$ is an extremal weight of $E$; write
$E^{*}=L(-w_0\nu)$ for its dual
([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).

With $\chi_\lambda,\chi_\mu$ the generalized central characters and
$\operatorname{pr}$ the exact central projections of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], define the **onto-wall** and
**out-of-wall** translations
$$T_{\mathrm{on}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\mu}\circ(E\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\lambda}},\qquad T_{\mathrm{out}}:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ(E^{*}\otimes-)\big|_{\mathcal O_{\chi_\mu}},$$
and the **wall-crossing functor**
$$\theta_s:=T_{\mathrm{out}}\circ T_{\mathrm{on}}\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$

**Basic properties.** Both translations are exact, and $T_{\mathrm{out}}$ is
both a left and a right adjoint of $T_{\mathrm{on}}$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]); hence
$\theta_s$ is exact and, as a composite of restriction-of-scalars and central
block projection applied to tensoring by $E^{*}\otimes E$, it is a natural
direct summand of the endofunctor
$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\circ((E^{*}\otimes E)\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_{\chi_\lambda}$,
so it is a projective functor on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]. On
standard objects the dominant-chamber counts are
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ and the
two-factor flag $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(w\cdot s\cdot\lambda)]$ for
$T_{\mathrm{out}}\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$, as follows directly from the tensor flag and the two norm bounds above.
Put $v=\lambda+\rho$, $u=\mu+\rho$. A retained onto-wall label satisfies
$wv+\gamma=xu$ with $|\gamma|\le|u-v|$. Thus
$|\gamma|=|v-w^{-1}xu|\ge|v-u|$; equality and regularity of $v$ give
$w^{-1}xu=u$, leaving the single label $w\cdot\mu$, with its extremal
weight of multiplicity one. For the return translation,
$wu+\delta=xv$ implies equality in $|u-w^{-1}xv|\ge|u-v|$, so
$w^{-1}xv\in\{v,sv\}$ and $x\in\{w,ws\}$, again with
extremal weights of multiplicity one. These calculations use the Verma
tensor flag of [[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]].

**Unit and counit.** The two tensor-block adjunctions supply natural
transformations
$$\eta\colon\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}\longrightarrow\theta_s,\qquad\varepsilon\colon\theta_s\longrightarrow\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal O_\lambda},$$
where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{on}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{out}}$
and $\varepsilon$ the counit of the adjunction $T_{\mathrm{out}}\dashv T_{\mathrm{on}}$;
each satisfies the triangle identities with its companion counit or unit on
the wall category, and these identities are part of the data. The pair
$(\theta_s,\eta,\varepsilon)$ is determined by the choice of the
biadjunction maps, which are fixed once and for all.

**Independence of the auxiliary weight.** Up to natural equivalence the
functor $\theta_s$ depends only on the wall $s$ and the block
$\mathcal O_\lambda$, not on the chosen ambient weight $\mu$: this
well-definedness statement is discharged forward by
[[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]],
which lifts the equality of the evaluations on standard objects to a natural
equivalence; it is recorded in `justified_by` and is not used to construct
$\theta_s$ or to generate objects.

**The bimodule.** Keep the ring $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with $\deg x_i=2$,
the simple reflections $s_i$ and the invariants $R^{s_i}$ of
[[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]], and recall that $R$ is
a graded $(R,R)$-bimodule and that shifts are defined as in
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]. For $1\le i\le n-1$ put
$$B_i:=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1),$$
the balanced tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]])
of the $(R,R^{s_i})$-bimodule $R$ with the $(R^{s_i},R)$-bimodule $R$, equipped
with the total internal grading of the tensor product and then shifted so that
$$(B_i)_d=\bigl(R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R\bigr)_{d+1}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z).$$
In the notation of Elias–Williamson the shift $(r)$ has $M(r)_d=M_{d+r}$, so
$M(1)_d=M_{d+1}$; in the library convention $M\{r\}_d=M_{d-r}$ this is
$M(1)=M\{-1\}$, i.e. $M(r)=M\{-r\}$ for every integer $r$. Both conventions
appear on this page, and every shifted formula is read through this dictionary;
when no ambiguity is possible we write $M(r)$.

**The two outer actions.** The left $R$-action is $r'(r\otimes r'')=r'r\otimes r''$
and the right $R$-action is $(r\otimes r'')r'=r\otimes r''r'$; both descend to
the balanced tensor product, they commute, they are homogeneous of degree $0$,
and they satisfy $R$-linearity on the relevant side, so $B_i$ is a graded
$(R,R)$-bimodule over $R^{s_i}$-balanced tensors. Explicitly, the $(R,R)$-bimodule
$B_i$ is generated by the two elements $1\otimes1$ and $1\otimes\alpha_i$, which
are homogeneous of degrees $-1$ and $+1$ respectively: $\alpha_i$ is a
degree-$2$ element of $R$ and the external shift moves degrees by $-1$.

**Elementary structure.** Since $2$ is invertible in $\mathbb Q$, we have the
decomposition $R=R^{s_i}\oplus\alpha_iR^{s_i}$ (the averaging idempotent
$\tfrac12(1+s_i)$ and its complement), so as a graded left $R$-module and again
as a graded right $R$-module
$$B_i\cong R(-1)\oplus R(1),$$
and $B_i$ is finite free of rank two on each side. The Demazure operator
$\partial_i$ of [[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]] is
$R^{s_i}$-linear and surjective onto $R^{s_i}$, and
$\partial_i(\alpha_i h)=2h$ for $h\in R^{s_i}$,
a fact used when the exact sequences of $B_i$ are displayed later on this page.

**Small $n$.** For $n=0$ or $n=1$ there are no simple reflections and no
$B_i$. The only word is the empty word, with bimodule $R$; the additive graded
Bott–Samelson category contains all finite direct sums of shifts of $R$ and
all degree-zero bimodule maps between them.

**Ambient bimodules.** Fix $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with $\deg x_i=2$ and
the simple reflections $s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}$ as in
[[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]]. We work inside the
category of graded $(R,R)$-bimodules and degree-zero bimodule maps, where
"graded" means a $\mathbb Z$-indexed direct sum decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ with $R_iM_jR_k\subseteq M_{i+j+k}$, and where
the internal shift $M\{r\}$ has $(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}$; as on the rest of this page
we also write $M(r):=M\{-r\}$ for the Elias–Williamson shift, so that
$M(1)_d=M_{d+1}$.

**Bott–Samelson objects.** For a finite word $\underline i=(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ let
$B_{\underline i}=B_{i_1}\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_RB_{i_r}$ be the Bott–Samelson
bimodule of [[def-bott-samelson-bimodule-of-a-word]], with
$B_{\emptyset}=R$. Let $\mathrm{BSBim}_n$ be the full subcategory of the ambient
category whose objects are the finite direct sums
$$B_{\underline i_1}(d_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus B_{\underline i_s}(d_s)$$
of shifts of Bott–Samelson bimodules, with the biproduct structure on direct
sums and degree-zero maps between them; the empty sum is the zero bimodule.
This is an additive $\mathbb Q$-linear category with grading shifts.
Its total graded morphism space
$\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(M,N)=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}^0(M,N(d))$
is an $R$-module by left multiplication on the output: a homogeneous scalar
of degree $a$ sends its degree-$d$ part to its degree-$(d+a)$ part. The
categorical morphisms are its degree-zero part, which need not be an
$R$-submodule. The tensor product over $R$
makes it a monoidal category with unit $R=B_{\emptyset}$, because the tensor
product of two finite sums of shifted Bott–Samelson products is again such a
sum, it distributes over the direct sums in each variable, and
$(M(d))\otimes_RN\cong M\otimes_R(N(d))\cong(M\otimes_RN)(d)$ naturally.

**Idempotent completion.** The type-A **Soergel category** is the idempotent
completion, in the sense of
[[def-the-idempotent-completion-of-a-preadditive-category]],
$$\mathrm{SBim}_n:=\mathrm{Kar}(\mathrm{BSBim}_n).$$
Its objects are the pairs $(M,e)$ with $M$ a finite sum of shifted
Bott–Samelson products and $e\in\operatorname{End}(M)$ a degree-zero idempotent,
and its morphisms are the degree-zero maps
$\operatorname{Hom}((M,e),(N,f))=f\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)e$. The tensor product
extends to the completion by $(M,e)\otimes_R(N,f):=(M\otimes_RN,e\otimes f)$ and
makes $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ a graded, additive, idempotent-complete monoidal
category with the same unit $R$; equivalently, $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ is the smallest
full subcategory of the ambient bimodule category that contains $R$ and the
$B_i$, is closed under finite direct sums, internal shifts, tensor products over
$R$, and direct summands. Every object of $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ is a finite direct
sum of graded shifts of indecomposable objects.

**Separation from the diagrammatic presentation.** We write
$\mathrm{SBim}_n$ for the bimodule category defined here and
$\mathcal D$ (or $\mathcal D_n$) for the $k$-linear graded monoidal category
presented by diagrams in
[[def-type-a-diagrammatic-soergel-category-and-its-bimodule-functor]]; the two
are related, but not identified, by the evaluation functor, which is proved to
be an equivalence only later on this page. In particular no statement about
$\mathcal D$ may be read as a statement about $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ before that
equivalence is established. For $n\le1$ there are no simple reflections, so the generating
object $R$ is the only indecomposable up to shift and $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ is the closure of
$R$ under finite direct sums, internal shifts and direct summands: its objects
are the finite direct sums of graded shifts of $R$, its morphisms are the graded
$R$-bimodule maps between them, and the summands are again finite sums of shifts
of $R$. Indeed a finite graded projective module over the connected
nonnegatively graded ring $R$ is graded free: lift a homogeneous basis modulo
$R_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}R_d$, obtaining a surjection from a finite graded free
module by graded Nakayama. Projectivity splits it; its kernel has zero
reduction modulo $R_+$ and is bounded below, so graded Nakayama kills the
kernel. This applies to every graded summand here, whose two $R$-actions agree.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

**The reduction.** Work over the ring $S=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ of the real
scalar-extension definition ([[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]]),
with $S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d$ the ideal of positive-degree elements; the residue
field of the right action is
$$k:=S/S_+=\mathbb R,$$
with quotient map $S\twoheadrightarrow k$, $s\mapsto \bar s$. For a graded
$(S,S)$-bimodule $M$ that is finite free as a right $S$-module put
$$\overline M:=M\otimes_Sk=M/MS_+,$$
the **reduction** of $M$: a finite-dimensional graded $k$-vector space, on which
the left $S$-action descends because $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $MS_+$ is
stable under left multiplication. Write $\overline M^{\,i}$ for its homogeneous
component of degree $i$, $d_i(M):=\dim_{\mathbb R}\overline M^{\,i}$ for the
graded dimensions, and
$$\dim\overline M:=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}d_i(M)\,v^{-i}$$
for the **graded dimension** (a finite Laurent polynomial); all tensor products
below are over $S$. For a morphism $f:M\to M'$ of graded bimodules, i.e. a
degree-zero bi-$S$-linear map, the induced map
$$\overline f:\overline M\to\overline{M'},\qquad \overline f(m+MS_+):=f(m)+M'S_+ ,$$
is well defined and $k$-linear of degree zero, because $f(MS_+)\subseteq M'S_+$.
Reduction is a functor from finite right-free graded bimodules to finite
dimensional graded $k$-vector spaces; it preserves finite direct sums and
shifts, in the sense $\overline{M(d)}=\overline M(d)$ in the Elias-Williamson
shift convention $M(d)_e=M_{d+e}$.

**The dominant Lefschetz operator.** Fix a strictly dominant degree-two
element
$$\rho=\sum_{j=1}^nc_jx_j\in S_2,\qquad c_1>c_2>\cdots>c_n ,$$
which exists by [[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]] (for
example $c_j=(n+1)/2-j$); recall that this is exactly the condition
$\rho(\alpha_i^\vee)>0$ for every simple coroot $\alpha_i^\vee$ in the
coordinate normalization of this page
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]]). Let
$\rho\cdot(-):M\to M$, $m\mapsto\rho m$, denote left multiplication by $\rho$.
Since $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $\rho\,(MS_+)\subseteq MS_+$, this
operator preserves the submodule $MS_+$ and therefore descends to a degree-two
$k$-linear endomorphism
$$L_0:=\rho\cdot(-):\overline M\longrightarrow\overline M,\qquad m+MS_+\longmapsto \rho m+MS_+,$$
called the **dominant Lefschetz operator** on $\overline M$. For rational
objects $B_x,B_s$ with real scalar extensions
$B_x^R=B_x\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$ and $B_s^R$, the same construction
applies to the reduced tensor product
$\overline{B_x^RB_s^R}=\overline{(B_xB_s)^R}$, where $B_xB_s$ denotes the
tensor product over the rational polynomial ring; the operator $L_0$ on it is
the value $\zeta=0$ of the deformed operator $L_\zeta$ defined later on this
page.

**Descent detection.** For every $w\in S_n$ and every simple reflection $s_i$
one has
$$(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \ell(s_iw)>\ell(w).$$
Indeed, $(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)=c_{w^{-1}(i)}-c_{w^{-1}(i+1)}$ is positive
exactly when $w^{-1}(i)<w^{-1}(i+1)$, the left-ascent criterion for inversion
length. Thus the displayed evaluation detects left descents; applied to
$w=x^{-1}$ it detects right descents of $x$, because $\ell(s_ix^{-1})=\ell(xs_i)$.

**Grading conventions.** The reduced module $\overline{B_x^R}$ has bottom degree
$-\ell(x)$ and top degree $+\ell(x)$; the unreduced bimodule has nonzero
components in arbitrarily high degrees. On a reduced module the "centered" degree $-i$ is the
internal degree $-i$, and the Lefschetz operator raises internal degree by two.
All homological (complex) shifts are written $[\,j\,]$ and all internal shifts
$(d)$, as on the rest of this page; the Bruhat order used throughout is the
rank-inequality order of
[[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]].

Both translations preserve the kernels of these quotient functors. For $T_{\mathrm{on}}$ this follows from step 1.1. For the return functor, $T_{\mathrm{on}}P_\lambda$ is projective-injective by [F3]. In the singular block its indecomposable summands are copies of $P_

Let $J$ be the ideal of $S^s$ generated by $S^W_+$. Then $I=SJ=J\oplus\alpha J$ under [F4], so $C=(S^s/J)\oplus\alpha(S^s/J)$ and averaging over $s$ identifies $S^s/J=C^s$. Thus $C$ is free over $C^s$ with generators in degrees $0,2$. The natural tensor map $S\otimes_{S^s}C\to C\otimes_{C^s}C$ is an isomorphism: its left $I$ acts as zero since the generators $S^W_+$ balance to zero on the right; factoring the left quotient and the image of $S^s$ therefore gives inverse maps on pure tensors. citations.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex
semisimple, $\lambda$ the dominant regular integral representative of a block
and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$.
Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan
reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then:

(1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
shifted by $\lambda+\rho$ in the published $\operatorname{HC}_\rho$ convention,
followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
(multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel;

(2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$
identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective,
canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its
isomorphism class;

(3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the
coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or
used.

This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral
case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the
invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block
with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor
$V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant
algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]],
so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$
and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map
$$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$
is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory
of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of
objects killed by $V$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory
([[def-axiom-of-choice]],
[[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]).

In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the
antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let
$$P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$
([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]); it is unique up to isomorphism and
indecomposable ([[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]],
[[def-projective-object]]), and it is an injective object of
$\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is
$$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-}\mathbf{mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$
with the left action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M)$ induced by composition on the right of
the source: $a\cdot f=f\circ a$
([[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]). Its
values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are
written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and
$VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$. The functor $V$ is exact, because
$P$ is projective, and hence left exact; the identity
$VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with its regular module structure
is the Yoneda identification. Replacing the chosen projective cover $P$ by an
isomorphic one changes $V$ by a natural equivalence of functors compatible
with the endomorphism-ring identification, so the construction depends only
on the isomorphism class of $P$.

**Well-definedness: $P$ is injective.** We prove that $P$ is an injective
object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ using only the listed suppliers, following the
argument of [Soe90, Sections 1.2 and 2.1] in its algebraic form. Put
$\eta:=-\rho$; then $W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, because $w\cdot\eta=w(\eta+\rho)-\rho=-\rho$
for every $w$ ([[cor-central-characters-are-dot-weyl-orbits]]). By
[[thm-simple-objects-of-category-o-are-highest-weight-modules]] the simple
objects are the $L(\mu)$ with $L(\mu)$ determined by $\mu$, and the composition
factors of $M(\eta)$ have highest weights in $W\cdot\eta\cap(\eta-Q^+)=\{\eta\}$;
hence $M(\eta)=L(\eta)$ is simple. By BGG reciprocity
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]) applied to the single-label block, and the existence
of Verma flags for projectives ([[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]]),
the projective cover $P(\eta)$ has a Verma flag with the single factor
$\Delta(\eta)=M(\eta)=L(\eta)$, so $P(\eta)\cong L(\eta)$; the block
$\mathcal O_\eta$ has a single simple object, which is projective, hence is
semisimple by enough projectives ([[thm-category-o-has-enough-projectives]]),
and therefore every object of $\mathcal O_\eta$, in particular $L(\eta)$, is
injective as well as projective in $\mathcal O_\eta$
([[def-injective-object]]). A projective object of a block is projective in
$\mathcal O$ ([[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]]), and an
injective object of a block is injective in $\mathcal O$ because the block
decomposition is a direct sum of abelian subcategories and the exact
projections restrict split exactness blockwise. Second, we identify a
projective-injective object
in the block $\mathcal O_\lambda$: let $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$ be the
finite-dimensional simple module of highest weight $\lambda+\rho$
([[thm-finite-dimensional-simple-modules-are-classified-by-dominant-highest-weights]])
and set
$$Q:=\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\lambda}\bigl(E\otimes L(\eta)\bigr)\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$
the exact central projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]].
Since $L(\eta)$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$, the tensor product
$E\otimes L(\eta)$ is projective and injective
([[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]]),
and its direct summand $Q$ is projective and injective in $\mathcal O$; the
general exact tensor-block biadjunction of
[[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] gives the
same conclusion with all adjoints and, by
[[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]],
injectivity (equivalently, $Q$ is a direct summand of a projective-injective
object, and injectivity passes to summands). Third, we compute a
one-dimensional Hom space: since $M(a)$ with $a=w_0\cdot\lambda$ is simple by
the same top-weight argument as for $\eta$ (every other highest weight in
$W\cdot a$ lies strictly above $a$ in the root order), the tensor product
$E^{*}\otimes M(a)$ has a finite Verma flag whose factors are the
$\Delta(a+\nu)$ with $\nu$ running through the weights of the dual module
$E^{*}$, by
[[lem-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-verma-flags]]; here
$E^{*}=L(-w_0(\lambda+\rho))$ ([[prop-highest-weight-of-the-dual-representation]]).
Projecting to the central character $\chi_\eta$ retains exactly the factors
with $a+\nu\in W\cdot\eta=\{\eta\}$, that is $\nu=-w_0(\lambda+\rho)$, the
highest weight of $E^{*}$ of multiplicity one, so
$$\operatorname{pr}_{\chi_\eta}\bigl(E^{*}\otimes M(a)\bigr)=L(\eta).$$
The tensor-hom adjunction and the tensor-block adjunction now give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,L(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),E^{*}\otimes M(a))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L(\eta),L(\eta))\cong\mathbb C,$$
because every homomorphism from the block-$\eta$ simple lands in the
$\chi_\eta$-summand and $L(\eta)$ is simple. Choose the nonzero, hence
surjective, element $q:Q\to L(a)$ and lift it through the projective cover
$P(a)\to L(a)$ to a map $Q\to P(a)$; its image is a submodule of $P(a)$
surjecting onto the head $L(a)$, hence is all of $P(a)$ by essentiality of a
projective cover, so the lift is surjective and splits by projectivity of
$P(a)$. Therefore $P(a)$ is a direct summand of the injective object $Q$
([[def-injective-object]]), and direct summands of injective objects are
injective, so $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is injective. This argument uses
[[thm-bgg-verma-homomorphism-criterion]] only through the standard embedding
criterion implicit in the top-weight computations, and it does not assume the
Endomorphismensatz.

**The once-each flag.** The tensor flag of $E\otimes M(-\rho)$ has labels
$-\rho+\gamma$ for weights $\gamma$ of $E=L(\lambda+\rho)$. Projection to
$\chi_\lambda$ keeps precisely $\gamma\in W(\lambda+\rho)$, each of
multiplicity one by [[lem-weight-norm-bound-for-finite-dimensional-simple-modules]].
Thus $Q$ has each $\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)$ once. Every such Verma contains
$M(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(a)$ by
[[lem-dominant-integral-dot-translates-embed-in-the-verma-module]]. BGG
reciprocity gives $(P(a):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))\ge1$; the splitting
$Q=P(a)\oplus Q'$ and
[[lem-direct-summands-of-verma-filtered-objects-are-verma-filtered]] give the
opposite bound one. Hence all these multiplicities equal one, $Q'$ has
an empty flag and is zero, and $Q=P(a)$. Since $P(a)$ is projective,
$V$ is exact and $\dim VX=[X:L(a)]$ for finite-length $X$: on simples its
values are $\mathbb C$ at the head label and zero otherwise. Consequently
$\dim V\Delta(x\cdot\lambda)=1$ for every $x$. Every simple submodule of a
Verma is itself a simple Verma: its universal Verma map into that Verma is
injective. Thus the unique simple standard $L(a)$ is its only possible
socle label, and [[thm-verma-homomorphism-spaces-have-dimension-at-most-one]]
makes this socle a single copy of $L(a)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a regular integral block and simple reflection
$s$, with $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$, there is a natural
isomorphism of functors to left $C$-modules
$$V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}V.$$
Equivalently the functor is tensoring by the $(C,C)$-bimodule
$C\otimes_{C^s}C$, with left action on the first factor and right action on the
second. In type A over $\mathbb C$, its polynomial lift is tensoring on the
left by $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$; read up to the auxiliary suspension
normalisation fixed by the rank-one case, the right origin reduction of $B_s$
is the two-dimensional module of centered degrees $-1,1$, for $M=S$ the
coinvariant reduction satisfies
$B_s\otimes_SC\cong(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)$ in the same normalisation, and
$B_s\otimes_S\mathbb C$ itself is not the bimodule $C\otimes_{C^s}C$: the
former has vector-space dimension two, whereas the latter has dimension
$2|W|$. Forgetting the grading gives the displayed category-$\mathcal O$
formula, and no grading on arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a dominant regular integral representative
$\lambda$ and a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, set
$\theta_{\underline w}=\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, so that the standards
follow right multiplication in word order. Then
$$\theta_{\underline w}\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)\oplus\bigoplus_{x<w}P(x\cdot\lambda)^{m_x},\qquad m_x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.$$
Its class is $(1+s_1)\cdots(1+s_k)$ under the standard class map, with actual
subexpression multiplicities. The BGG matrix satisfies
$(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]$,
vanishes unless $y\le x$ in the Bruhat order, and has diagonal entries one.
Hence the top summand $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ occurs once and is the only summand
whose flag contains $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$; the remaining multiplicities are
determined by this triangular matrix and the product class. Consequently every
indecomposable projective is a summand of a word of wall crossings applied to
$\Delta(\lambda)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. In a regular integral block with dominant
representative $\lambda$:

1. Projective functors form a Krull-Schmidt category.
2. Their indecomposables are indexed by $W$, with $\Theta_w$ characterized by
$\Theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\cong P(w\cdot\lambda)$. For a reduced word
$w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the functor $\Theta_w$ is a multiplicity-one summand of
$\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}$, and every other indecomposable summand has a
label $x<w$. In particular every indecomposable projective functor is generated
as a summand by wall crossings.
3. Two projective functors are naturally equivalent exactly when their induced
operators on the Grothendieck group agree.

The characterization concerns evaluation on the dominant projective Verma; no
faithfulness of that evaluation on all natural maps of arbitrary
endofunctors is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$R=S(\mathfrak h)_{(0)}$ the localization at the origin, and use the selected
component $\mathcal D_R^{[\lambda]}(\lambda)$ of the tensor-generated deformed
family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]]. For
every $x\in W$ there is a projective $P_R(x,\lambda)$ in the deformed
$\lambda$-block whose residue fiber is $P(x\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to
isomorphism, and every indecomposable of this selected tensor component is one
of these lifts. Each lift has a finite deformed Verma flag with the same
multiplicities as its closed fiber. More generally, a finite projective in this
block is a direct summand of a finite sum of truncated induced projectives
representing relative weight spaces; for every map of deformation algebras
$R\to R'$ its base change is projective in the corresponding truncated category
and
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(P,N)\otimes_RR'\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{R'}}(P\otimes_RR',N\otimes_RR').$$
For a finite Verma-filtered target $N$ this Hom module is finite free over
local $R$. A $\mathfrak g\otimes R$-linear map between such finite
projective/Verma-filtered objects whose residue fiber is an isomorphism is
itself an isomorphism, weight by weight. For a dot-dominant integral target
$\nu$, including singular $\nu$, the same local projective construction gives
all lifts in its deformed block, with labels the distinct cosets $W/W_\nu$;
these lifts belong to the target component $\mathcal D_R^{[\nu]}(\lambda)$ of a
regular-source tensor family. It is neither necessary nor asserted that the
singular Verma itself generates every target projective, and the other central
components of the full tensor family are not claimed to have only these
indecomposables.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant regular integral,
$S=S(\mathfrak h)$, $R=S_{(0)}$, and $P_R=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed
antidominant projective. Write $\operatorname{HC}_\rho\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to S^W$
for the published shifted Harish-Chandra isomorphism,
$\sigma_\lambda(f)(\epsilon)=f(\lambda+\rho+\epsilon)$, and define
$$a_\lambda\colon Z\otimes_{\mathbb C}R\longrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R,\qquad z\otimes r\longmapsto\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))\otimes r.$$
Then $a_\lambda$ and the action map $Z\otimes R\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)$
are surjective and have the same kernel, inducing a canonical $R$-algebra
isomorphism
$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes R}(P_R)\cong R\otimes_{R^W}R.$$
On a generic Verma constituent of highest weight $x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon$, $z$
acts by the scalar
$\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(x(\lambda+\rho)+\epsilon)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(x^{-1}\epsilon)$;
these scalars vary with $x$, and the center need not act by a single scalar on
$P_R$. After tensoring the right $R$ factor with the residue field at $0$, the
endomorphism algebra becomes $C=S/(S^W_+S)$. More generally, for dot-dominant
integral $\nu$ the corresponding algebra is $R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R$, where
$W_\nu$ is the dot stabilizer. Translation out of that facet identifies the
singular antidominant projective with the regular one; under these shifted
Harish-Chandra identifications, its induced endomorphism map is the inclusion
$R^{W_\nu}\otimes_{R^W}R\hookrightarrow R\otimes_{R^W}R$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every
finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ the
translation functor $T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$
([[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]) is exact, and
$T_{\chi',E^*,\chi}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of
$T_{\chi,E,\chi'}$; in particular both functors send projectives to
projectives and injectives to injectives. Consequently, in the setting of
[[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], $T_\mu^\lambda$ is both a left
and a right adjoint of $T_\lambda^\mu$, and the two functors are exact.

**The bimodule.** Keep the ring $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with $\deg x_i=2$,
the simple reflections $s_i$ and the invariants $R^{s_i}$ of
[[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]], and recall that $R$ is
a graded $(R,R)$-bimodule and that shifts are defined as in
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]. For $1\le i\le n-1$ put
$$B_i:=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1),$$
the balanced tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]])
of the $(R,R^{s_i})$-bimodule $R$ with the $(R^{s_i},R)$-bimodule $R$, equipped
with the total internal grading of the tensor product and then shifted so that
$$(B_i)_d=\bigl(R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R\bigr)_{d+1}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z).$$
In the notation of Elias–Williamson the shift $(r)$ has $M(r)_d=M_{d+r}$, so
$M(1)_d=M_{d+1}$; in the library convention $M\{r\}_d=M_{d-r}$ this is
$M(1)=M\{-1\}$, i.e. $M(r)=M\{-r\}$ for every integer $r$. Both conventions
appear on this page, and every shifted formula is read through this dictionary;
when no ambiguity is possible we write $M(r)$.

**The two outer actions.** The left $R$-action is $r'(r\otimes r'')=r'r\otimes r''$
and the right $R$-action is $(r\otimes r'')r'=r\otimes r''r'$; both descend to
the balanced tensor product, they commute, they are homogeneous of degree $0$,
and they satisfy $R$-linearity on the relevant side, so $B_i$ is a graded
$(R,R)$-bimodule over $R^{s_i}$-balanced tensors. Explicitly, the $(R,R)$-bimodule
$B_i$ is generated by the two elements $1\otimes1$ and $1\otimes\alpha_i$, which
are homogeneous of degrees $-1$ and $+1$ respectively: $\alpha_i$ is a
degree-$2$ element of $R$ and the external shift moves degrees by $-1$.

**Elementary structure.** Since $2$ is invertible in $\mathbb Q$, we have the
decomposition $R=R^{s_i}\oplus\alpha_iR^{s_i}$ (the averaging idempotent
$\tfrac12(1+s_i)$ and its complement), so as a graded left $R$-module and again
as a graded right $R$-module
$$B_i\cong R(-1)\oplus R(1),$$
and $B_i$ is finite free of rank two on each side. The Demazure operator
$\partial_i$ of [[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]] is
$R^{s_i}$-linear and surjective onto $R^{s_i}$, and
$\partial_i(\alpha_i h)=2h$ for $h\in R^{s_i}$,
a fact used when the exact sequences of $B_i$ are displayed later on this page.

**Small $n$.** For $n=0$ or $n=1$ there are no simple reflections and no
$B_i$. The only word is the empty word, with bimodule $R$; the additive graded
Bott–Samelson category contains all finite direct sums of shifts of $R$ and
all degree-zero bimodule maps between them.

**Ambient bimodules.** Fix $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with $\deg x_i=2$ and
the simple reflections $s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}$ as in
[[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]]. We work inside the
category of graded $(R,R)$-bimodules and degree-zero bimodule maps, where
"graded" means a $\mathbb Z$-indexed direct sum decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ with $R_iM_jR_k\subseteq M_{i+j+k}$, and where
the internal shift $M\{r\}$ has $(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}$; as on the rest of this page
we also write $M(r):=M\{-r\}$ for the Elias–Williamson shift, so that
$M(1)_d=M_{d+1}$.

**Bott–Samelson objects.** For a finite word $\underline i=(i_1,\ldots,i_r)$ let
$B_{\underline i}=B_{i_1}\otimes_R\cdots\otimes_RB_{i_r}$ be the Bott–Samelson
bimodule of [[def-bott-samelson-bimodule-of-a-word]], with
$B_{\emptyset}=R$. Let $\mathrm{BSBim}_n$ be the full subcategory of the ambient
category whose objects are the finite direct sums
$$B_{\underline i_1}(d_1)\oplus\cdots\oplus B_{\underline i_s}(d_s)$$
of shifts of Bott–Samelson bimodules, with the biproduct structure on direct
sums and degree-zero maps between them; the empty sum is the zero bimodule.
This is an additive $\mathbb Q$-linear category with grading shifts.
Its total graded morphism space
$\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(M,N)=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}\operatorname{Hom}^0(M,N(d))$
is an $R$-module by left multiplication on the output: a homogeneous scalar
of degree $a$ sends its degree-$d$ part to its degree-$(d+a)$ part. The
categorical morphisms are its degree-zero part, which need not be an
$R$-submodule. The tensor product over $R$
makes it a monoidal category with unit $R=B_{\emptyset}$, because the tensor
product of two finite sums of shifted Bott–Samelson products is again such a
sum, it distributes over the direct sums in each variable, and
$(M(d))\otimes_RN\cong M\otimes_R(N(d))\cong(M\otimes_RN)(d)$ naturally.

**Idempotent completion.** The type-A **Soergel category** is the idempotent
completion, in the sense of
[[def-the-idempotent-completion-of-a-preadditive-category]],
$$\mathrm{SBim}_n:=\mathrm{Kar}(\mathrm{BSBim}_n).$$
Its objects are the pairs $(M,e)$ with $M$ a finite sum of shifted
Bott–Samelson products and $e\in\operatorname{End}(M)$ a degree-zero idempotent,
and its morphisms are the degree-zero maps
$\operatorname{Hom}((M,e),(N,f))=f\operatorname{Hom}(M,N)e$. The tensor product
extends to the completion by $(M,e)\otimes_R(N,f):=(M\otimes_RN,e\otimes f)$ and
makes $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ a graded, additive, idempotent-complete monoidal
category with the same unit $R$; equivalently, $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ is the smallest
full subcategory of the ambient bimodule category that contains $R$ and the
$B_i$, is closed under finite direct sums, internal shifts, tensor products over
$R$, and direct summands. Every object of $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ is a finite direct
sum of graded shifts of indecomposable objects.

**Separation from the diagrammatic presentation.** We write
$\mathrm{SBim}_n$ for the bimodule category defined here and
$\mathcal D$ (or $\mathcal D_n$) for the $k$-linear graded monoidal category
presented by diagrams in
[[def-type-a-diagrammatic-soergel-category-and-its-bimodule-functor]]; the two
are related, but not identified, by the evaluation functor, which is proved to
be an equivalence only later on this page. In particular no statement about
$\mathcal D$ may be read as a statement about $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ before that
equivalence is established. For $n\le1$ there are no simple reflections, so the generating
object $R$ is the only indecomposable up to shift and $\mathrm{SBim}_n$ is the closure of
$R$ under finite direct sums, internal shifts and direct summands: its objects
are the finite direct sums of graded shifts of $R$, its morphisms are the graded
$R$-bimodule maps between them, and the summands are again finite sums of shifts
of $R$. Indeed a finite graded projective module over the connected
nonnegatively graded ring $R$ is graded free: lift a homogeneous basis modulo
$R_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}R_d$, obtaining a surjection from a finite graded free
module by graded Nakayama. Projectivity splits it; its kernel has zero
reduction modulo $R_+$ and is bounded below, so graded Nakayama kills the
kernel. This applies to every graded summand here, whose two $R$-actions agree.

**Graphs and supports.** Keep $k=\mathbb Q$, $R=\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with
$\deg x_i=2$, and the affine scheme $V=\mathbb A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}R$,
whose $k$-points are $V(k)=k^n$. Use the place-permuting action of $S_n$
from [[def-type-a-reflection-realization-and-polynomial-ring]].
For $w\in S_n$ let
$$Gr(w):=\operatorname{Graph}(w:V\to V)\subseteq V\times_kV,\quad Gr(w)(k)=\{(w\lambda,\lambda):\lambda\in k^n\},\qquad Gr(A):=\bigcup_{w\in A}Gr(w)\ \ (A\subseteq S_n),$$
so that $V\times_kV=\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kR)$ and $Gr(w)$ is the graph
of the map $\lambda\mapsto w\lambda$. A graded $(R,R)$-bimodule $M$ is the
same thing as a graded module over $R\otimes_kR$, and the support of $m\in M$ is
the zero set $\operatorname{supp}(m):=V(\operatorname{Ann}(m))\subseteq V\times V$
of its annihilator ideal in $R\otimes_kR$. For $A\subseteq S_n$ put
$$\Gamma_AM:=\{m\in M:\operatorname{supp}(m)\subseteq Gr(A)\},$$
a graded sub-bimodule of $M$. Since $Gr(A)$ is closed with radical ideal
$I(Gr(A))=\bigcap_{w\in A}I(Gr(w))$ (an intersection of prime ideals, since each
$Gr(w)$ is a linear subspace of $V\times V$ complementing the second factor), an
element $m$ lies in $\Gamma_AM$ exactly when $I(Gr(A))^N m=0$ for some $N\ge0$:
this is the Nullstellensatz together with the Noetherianity of
$R\otimes_kR$. The ideal itself need not annihilate such an element — in
$(R\otimes_kR)/I(Gr(e))^2$ the class of $1$ is supported on $Gr(e)$ but is not
killed by $I(Gr(e))$ — which is why the criterion is stated with a power of the
ideal. For $i\in\mathbb Z$ we write
$$\Gamma_{\ge i}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\ell(x)\ge i\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{\le i}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\ell(x)\le i\}}M,$$
using the length function of [[lem-type-a-reduced-words-are-connected-by-braid-moves]],
while for $y\in S_n$ the $y$-indexed symbols denote the *Bruhat
principal-set* cutoffs of Soergel's Notation 6.1,
$$\Gamma_{\le y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x\le y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{<y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x<y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{\ge y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x\ge y\}}M,\qquad \Gamma_{>y}M:=\Gamma_{\{x:\,x>y\}}M,$$
with $\Gamma_yM:=\Gamma_{\{y\}}M$ the elements concentrated on the single graph
$Gr(y)$ and $\Gamma_{\ne y}M:=\Gamma_{S_n\setminus\{y\}}M$ the elements
concentrated off $Gr(y)$. The integer-indexed symbols of the previous display are
the *length* cutoffs used to define the flags below, and they must not be
confused with the element-indexed Bruhat cutoffs: for $y=s_1$ in $S_4$ the
submodule $\Gamma_{\le1}M$ contains $Gr(s_3)$ while
$\Gamma_{\le y}M=\Gamma_{\{e,s_1\}}M$ does not, and the two cutoffs agree at
the extremes, $\Gamma_{\le w_0}=\Gamma_{\le\ell(w_0)}=M$ and
$\Gamma_{<e}=\Gamma_{\le-1}=0$. So
$\Gamma^yM:=M/\Gamma_{\ne y}M$ is Soergel's $y$-layer
*quotient*; following Soergel's
Notation 6.1 we write the two $y$-layer quotients with an underline,
$$\underline{\Gamma}_{\le y}M:=\Gamma_{\le y}M/\Gamma_{<y}M,\qquad \underline{\Gamma}_{\ge y}M:=\Gamma_{\ge y}M/\Gamma_{>y}M,$$
so that $\underline{\Gamma}_{\le y}M$ is the quotient of the lower support
submodule by $\Gamma_{<y}M$ and $\underline{\Gamma}_{\ge y}M$ the quotient of
the upper support submodule by the part supported strictly above $Gr(y)$.

**Standard bimodules.** For $w\in S_n$ let $R_w$ be the graded $(R,R)$-bimodule
which equals $R$ as a graded $k$-vector space and has
$$f\cdot x=fx,\qquad x\cdot g=w(g)\,x\qquad(f,g,x\in R),$$
where $w(g)(\lambda):=g(w^{-1}\lambda)$; $R_w$ is generated by the element $1$ of
degree $0$. Write $(k)$ for the *external* shift $M(k):=M\{-k\}$ of
[[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]], so that
$M(k)_d=M_{d+k}$; this is the shift convention of the type-A sources, and it is
the one in which $B_i=R\otimes_{R^{s_i}}R(1)$ of
[[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]] has $1\otimes1$ of
degree $-1$. Put
$$\Delta_w(d):=R_w(d-\ell(w)),\qquad \nabla_w(d):=R_w(d+\ell(w))\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$
so that $\Delta_w(d)$ is the standard bimodule $R_w$ with its generator in
degree $\ell(w)-d$, and $\nabla_w(d)$ is $R_w$ with its generator in degree
$-\ell(w)-d$. Thus $\Delta_w(0)=R_w\{\ell(w)\}$,
$\nabla_w(0)=R_w\{-\ell(w)\}$ and $\Delta_e(d)=\nabla_e(d)=R(d)$ is generated
in degree $-d$; in particular $\Delta_e(0)=\nabla_e(0)=R_e=R$.

For graded free $R$-modules in this type-A page, a homogeneous free generator of degree $a$ contributes $v^a$ to graded rank. This is the $v\mapsto v^{-1}$ transform of Soergel's rank convention in his Notation 5.2; all rank formulas below use this convention.

**Support filtrations.** A $\Delta$-flag of a graded $R$-bimodule $M$ is a
finite chain $0=M_0\subseteq M_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq M_k=M$ of graded
sub-bimodules which refines the length filtration
$$M=\Gamma_{\ge0}M\supseteq\Gamma_{\ge1}M\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\Gamma_{\ge\ell(w_0)+1}M=0$$
of $M$ (here $\Gamma_{\ge0}M=M$ for every bimodule supported on
$Gr(S_n)=\bigcup_{w}Gr(w)$, which all bimodules of this page are, and
$\Gamma_{\ge i}M=0$ for $i>\ell(w_0)$ because no graph $Gr(x)$ with
$\ell(x)>i$ remains) and whose successive quotients are
standard bimodules $M_j/M_{j-1}\cong R_{x_j}\{a_j\}$. We require each
length layer to be a finite direct sum of shifted graph bimodules of that
length, as in Soergel's Definition 5.4. Thus the
quotients carry a numbering with $\ell(x_1)\ge\cdots\ge\ell(x_k)$ and each
$R_{x_j}\{a_j\}$ is one graph, so that $M$ has a "support flag" in the sense of
Soergel's $F_\Delta$. A $\nabla$-flag has the same direct-sum condition on its length layers, with the reverse length
filtration $\Gamma_{\le i}M$ and $\ell(x_1)\le\cdots\le\ell(x_k)$. The
refinement condition is a condition on supports, not an ordering of incomparable
quotients of equal length; only the lengths are ordered. For $i=\ell(x)$ the
graded multiplicity is
$$(M:\Delta_x(d)):=\text{multiplicity of }\Delta_x(d)\text{ in } \Gamma_{\ge i}M/\Gamma_{\ge i+1}M,$$
and, for a $\nabla$-flag, $(M:\nabla_x(d))$ is the multiplicity of
$\nabla_x(d)$ in $\Gamma_{\le i}M/\Gamma_{\le i-1}M$; a priori both symbols
refer to a chosen compatible enumeration (the next items on this page prove that
they do not depend on it). With $T_x$ the Hecke basis of
[[lem-type-a-hecke-standard-basis-for-soergel-comparison]] and
$\widetilde T_x:=v^{\ell(x)}T_x$, the character sums attached to a flag are
$$h_\Delta(M):=\sum_{x,d}(M:\Delta_x(d))\,v^d\,\widetilde T_x,\qquad h_\nabla(M):=\sum_{x,d}(M:\nabla_x(d))\,v^{-d}\,\widetilde T_x,$$
and they are used only through the items that prove these sums intrinsic.

**Small $n$.** For $n\le1$ there is a single element $e$ and every object is a finite direct sum of shifts $\bigoplus_j R(d_j)$. Its one-graph flags have these summands as quotients, so $h_\Delta=\sum_jv^{d_j}\widetilde T_e$ and $h_\nabla=\sum_jv^{-d_j}\widetilde T_e$; in particular both characters send the unit $R$ to $1$.

**The reduction.** Work over the ring $S=\mathbb R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ of the real
scalar-extension definition ([[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]]),
with $S_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}S_d$ the ideal of positive-degree elements; the residue
field of the right action is
$$k:=S/S_+=\mathbb R,$$
with quotient map $S\twoheadrightarrow k$, $s\mapsto \bar s$. For a graded
$(S,S)$-bimodule $M$ that is finite free as a right $S$-module put
$$\overline M:=M\otimes_Sk=M/MS_+,$$
the **reduction** of $M$: a finite-dimensional graded $k$-vector space, on which
the left $S$-action descends because $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $MS_+$ is
stable under left multiplication. Write $\overline M^{\,i}$ for its homogeneous
component of degree $i$, $d_i(M):=\dim_{\mathbb R}\overline M^{\,i}$ for the
graded dimensions, and
$$\dim\overline M:=\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}d_i(M)\,v^{-i}$$
for the **graded dimension** (a finite Laurent polynomial); all tensor products
below are over $S$. For a morphism $f:M\to M'$ of graded bimodules, i.e. a
degree-zero bi-$S$-linear map, the induced map
$$\overline f:\overline M\to\overline{M'},\qquad \overline f(m+MS_+):=f(m)+M'S_+ ,$$
is well defined and $k$-linear of degree zero, because $f(MS_+)\subseteq M'S_+$.
Reduction is a functor from finite right-free graded bimodules to finite
dimensional graded $k$-vector spaces; it preserves finite direct sums and
shifts, in the sense $\overline{M(d)}=\overline M(d)$ in the Elias-Williamson
shift convention $M(d)_e=M_{d+e}$.

**The dominant Lefschetz operator.** Fix a strictly dominant degree-two
element
$$\rho=\sum_{j=1}^nc_jx_j\in S_2,\qquad c_1>c_2>\cdots>c_n ,$$
which exists by [[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]] (for
example $c_j=(n+1)/2-j$); recall that this is exactly the condition
$\rho(\alpha_i^\vee)>0$ for every simple coroot $\alpha_i^\vee$ in the
coordinate normalization of this page
([[def-finite-weyl-root-system-lattice-and-chamber-conventions]]). Let
$\rho\cdot(-):M\to M$, $m\mapsto\rho m$, denote left multiplication by $\rho$.
Since $S_+\subseteq S$ is central and $\rho\,(MS_+)\subseteq MS_+$, this
operator preserves the submodule $MS_+$ and therefore descends to a degree-two
$k$-linear endomorphism
$$L_0:=\rho\cdot(-):\overline M\longrightarrow\overline M,\qquad m+MS_+\longmapsto \rho m+MS_+,$$
called the **dominant Lefschetz operator** on $\overline M$. For rational
objects $B_x,B_s$ with real scalar extensions
$B_x^R=B_x\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb R$ and $B_s^R$, the same construction
applies to the reduced tensor product
$\overline{B_x^RB_s^R}=\overline{(B_xB_s)^R}$, where $B_xB_s$ denotes the
tensor product over the rational polynomial ring; the operator $L_0$ on it is
the value $\zeta=0$ of the deformed operator $L_\zeta$ defined later on this
page.

**Descent detection.** For every $w\in S_n$ and every simple reflection $s_i$
one has
$$(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \ell(s_iw)>\ell(w).$$
Indeed, $(w\rho)(\alpha_i^\vee)=c_{w^{-1}(i)}-c_{w^{-1}(i+1)}$ is positive
exactly when $w^{-1}(i)<w^{-1}(i+1)$, the left-ascent criterion for inversion
length. Thus the displayed evaluation detects left descents; applied to
$w=x^{-1}$ it detects right descents of $x$, because $\ell(s_ix^{-1})=\ell(xs_i)$.

**Grading conventions.** The reduced module $\overline{B_x^R}$ has bottom degree
$-\ell(x)$ and top degree $+\ell(x)$; the unreduced bimodule has nonzero
components in arbitrarily high degrees. On a reduced module the "centered" degree $-i$ is the
internal degree $-i$, and the Lefschetz operator raises internal degree by two.
All homological (complex) shifts are written $[\,j\,]$ and all internal shifts
$(d)$, as on the rest of this page; the Bruhat order used throughout is the
rank-inequality order of
[[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]].

Over $k=\mathbb Q$ or $k=\mathbb R$, the bimodule Soergel category has unique finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions. For every $x\in S_n$ there is a unique normalized indecomposable $B_x$ supported on $\{y:y\le x\}$ with top $\Delta$ layer exactly $\Delta_x=R_x(-\ell(x))$. It is the unique summand with the $x$ graph of any reduced Bott-Samelson word for $x$. Every indecomposable is exactly one $B_x(d)$. Its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local, with residue field $k$ under restriction to its rank-one top layer. No Kazhdan-Lusztig character identity is assumed.

Over $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$, let $B_x$ be the normalized indecomposable bimodule classified by its top support. With right dual $DM=\operatorname{Hom}_{-R}^{\bullet}(M,R)$, one has $DB_x\cong B_x$. Its right reduction has degrees only in $[-\ell(x),\ell(x)]$, all congruent to $\ell(x)$ modulo two, and the two extremal dimensions are one. Hence its reduced graded dimensions are symmetric. Every Bott-Samelson word has a graded perfect symmetric invariant trace form. These assertions assume neither the Kazhdan-Lusztig character conjecture nor hard Lefschetz.

Let $B_w$ be the rational indecomposable type-A Soergel bimodule and let $B_w^R$ be its real scalar extension. (1) $B_w^R$ is indecomposable; its finite-dimensional degree-zero endomorphism algebra is local with residue field $\mathbb R$. If $S(w)$ holds, its degree-zero endomorphism algebra is $\mathbb R$, but no rank-one assertion for the full graded endomorphism module is made. (2) Real extension preserves the labels and shifts of all finite Krull-Schmidt decompositions of rational Soergel bimodules, and every real indecomposable is a unique $B_w^R(d)$. (3) $\Delta$/$\nabla$ support-filtration multiplicities, characters, reduction by positive-degree right polynomials, and Hom spaces commute with scalar extension; thus character identities over $\mathbb R$ descend to $\mathbb Q$. (4) If $xs>x$ and $S(y)$ holds for all $y<xs$, then $B_xB_s=B_{xs}\oplus\bigoplus_{y<xs}B_y^{a_y}$ with $a_y$ nonnegative integers and no grading shifts; the top summand occurs once. If $xs<x$ and $S(x)$ holds, then $B_xB_s=B_x(1)\oplus B_x(-1)$. All assertions concern the normalized self-dual indecomposables.

**The Bott-Samelson bimodule and its subexpression basis.** Fix a finite word
$\underline x=s_1\cdots s_m$ in the simple reflections and let
$$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x):=B_{s_1}\otimes_S\cdots\otimes_SB_{s_m}$$
be the real Bott-Samelson bimodule
([[def-bott-samelson-bimodule-of-a-word]]), with $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$
([[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]]). In each factor put
$$c_{\mathrm{id}}:=1\otimes1,\qquad c_s:=\tfrac12\bigl(\alpha_s\otimes1+1\otimes\alpha_s\bigr),$$
of degrees $-1$ and $+1$; here $\alpha_s$ is the coordinate root of
[[def-real-type-a-soergel-category-and-scalar-extension]], so that
$\partial_s(r)=(r-sr)/\alpha_s$ is the coordinate Demazure operator. The
elements $\{c_{\mathrm{id}},c_s\}$ form a right (and a left) $S$-basis of $B_s$
and the multiplication rules
$$c_{\mathrm{id}}c_{\mathrm{id}}=c_{\mathrm{id}},\qquad c_{\mathrm{id}}c_s=c_s,\qquad c_sc_s=c_s\alpha_s$$
hold. For a subexpression $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_m)$
with $\varepsilon_i\in\{\mathrm{id},s_i\}$ put
$$c_\varepsilon:=c_{\varepsilon_1}\cdots c_{\varepsilon_m}\in\mathrm{BS}(\underline x),$$
the tensor product of the chosen elements, and put
$$c_{\mathrm{top}}:=c_{s_1}\cdots c_{s_m}.$$
The elements $\{c_\varepsilon\}$ form a right (and a left) $S$-basis of
$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)$; the bimodule is finite free of rank $2^m$ on each
side ([[lem-type-a-soergel-generators-are-finite-free-on-both-sides]]).
Moreover $\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)\cong\bigl(S\otimes_{S^{s_1}}S\otimes_{S^{s_2}}\cdots\otimes_{S^{s_m}}S\bigr)(m)$,
so after the shift by $(-m)$ the termwise multiplication makes
$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)(-m)$ a commutative ring with unit $c_{\mathrm{id}}\cdots c_{\mathrm{id}}$;
in particular it contains the powers of any degree-two element and products of
commuting elements.

**The trace and the intersection form.** Define the **trace**
$$\operatorname{Tr}:\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)\longrightarrow S$$
to be the coefficient of $c_{\mathrm{top}}$ when an element is written in the
right basis $\{c_\varepsilon\}$, and define the **intersection form** by
$$\langle b,b'\rangle:=\operatorname{Tr}(b\,b'),$$
the product being taken in the commutative ring $\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)(-m)$.
Then:

1. $\langle-,-\rangle$ is a graded symmetric form, $S$-bilinear for the right
   action, and invariant in the sense
   $\langle rb,b'\rangle=\langle b,rb'\rangle$ and
   $\langle br,b'\rangle=\langle b,b'r\rangle=\langle b,b'\rangle r$ for
   $r\in S$;
2. if $B$ is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of
   Bott-Samelson bimodules, then an invariant form on $B$ is obtained by
   restricting an invariant form of the ambient finite sum, and the restriction
   is determined up to the choices of the ambient forms;
3. for a self-dual bimodule $B$ with invariant form $\langle-,-\rangle_B$ the
   **induced form** on $BB_s$ is the unique invariant form satisfying, for all
   $b,b'\in B$,
   $$\langle\alpha(b),\alpha(b')\rangle=\partial_s(\langle b,b'\rangle_B),\qquad \langle\alpha(b),\beta(b')\rangle=\langle b,b'\rangle_B=\langle\beta(b),\alpha(b')\rangle,\qquad \langle\beta(b),\beta(b')\rangle=\langle b,b'\rangle_B\,\alpha_s,$$
   where $\alpha(b):=b\,c_{\mathrm{id}}$ and $\beta(b):=b\,c_s$;
4. the intersection form on a Bott-Samelson bimodule is non-degenerate as an
   $S$-valued form, and for a summand $B$ of a Bott-Samelson bimodule the
   restricted form is non-degenerate whenever $B$ has finite free right
   $S$-rank and the induced reduced form on $\overline B$ is non-degenerate
   (graded Nakayama);
5. the reduction of $\langle-,-\rangle$ is a graded symmetric $k$-valued form
   $\langle-,-\rangle_{\overline M}$ on $\overline M$
   ([[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]]), and for a
   finite right-free $M$ the $S$-valued form is non-degenerate if and only if
   the reduced form is graded non-degenerate;
6. Bott-Samelson bimodules and the indecomposable bimodules $B_w^R$ are
   self-dual, so
   $\dim(\overline{B_w^R})^{-i}=\dim(\overline{B_w^R})^{i}$ for all $i$
   (symmetric Betti numbers).

Additionally record the left/right asymmetry: the form is bilinear for the
right action and satisfies the two invariance identities displayed in (1); it is
not left $S$-bilinear in general, because $\langle rb,b'\rangle$ is defined
through the trace of a product while the two $S$-actions differ on
$\mathrm{BS}(\underline x)$.

Let $R$ be a nonzero unital ring. Then $R$ is semisimple if and only if $$R\cong\prod_{i=1}^rM_{n_i}(D_i)$$ for positive integers $r,n_i$ and division rings $D_i$. See [[thm-endomorphism-ring-of-the-left-regular-module-is-opposite]].
